description.en: Pick a sample of the month's A2 flights and compare each track with its log and site plan: was the planned distance kept, was every sub-30 m segment flown in low-speed mode with an evaluation made beforehand, and did the aircraft pass over any area where uninvolved people were present? Raise a finding for each breach and follow it to closure.

evidenceHint.en: Monthly sample worksheet listing flights reviewed, distance kept, low-speed segments checked and findings raised

text.en: Select at least five A2 flights from the month, covering more than one pilot where possible.
Check each sub-30 m segment for low-speed mode and an evaluation dated before it.
Overlay the track on the site plan and look for passes over occupied areas.
Raise a finding for every breach and name an owner and a due date.
File the worksheet and carry open findings into next month's sample.

templates.title: A2 certificate of remote pilot competency
templates.description: An A2 pilot holds the certificate of remote pilot competency, obtained in the order UAS.OPEN.030(2) sets: the A1/A3 online exam, practical self-training in A3 conditions, a declaration of that training and an extra theory exam.
templates.objective: To ensure every pilot who flies in A2 earned the A2 certificate in the prescribed order, holds it valid and carries it on every A2 flight.
templates.successCriteria:
Every A2 pilot has a valid A2 certificate from the competent authority or a designated or recognised entity on file.
Every A2 pilot has an A1/A3 proof dated before their declaration of practical self-training.
Every declaration is backed by a self-training log on a C2-like aircraft, covering manual and automated modes where the aircraft has both.
Every A2 flight log confirms the certificate was carried, and no pilot without one was assigned to A2 work.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the A2 pilot roster with A1/A3 proofs, self-training logs, declarations and A2 certificates.
Obtain A2 flight logs and rostering records for the period.
Obtain the exam results showing the number of questions and the score for each A2 exam.

Analysis:
For each A2 pilot, compare the dates of the A1/A3 proof, the self-training, the declaration and the A2 exam and confirm they follow the order UAS.OPEN.030(2) sets.
Read each self-training log for the aircraft used and the exercises flown, against AMC1 and AMC2 UAS.OPEN.030(2)(b).
Check each certificate's issuer and validity on the dates the pilot flew A2.
Confirm each exam result shows at least 30 questions and a score of at least 75%.
Search rostering and flight logs for A2 flights by pilots without a valid certificate, and check sampled logs for the certificate carried.

Output:
A list of A2 pilots whose steps are out of order or undocumented.
Any self-training log that does not show a C2-like aircraft or omits a control mode.
Any A2 flight by a pilot without a valid certificate or without it carried.

title.en: Plan each A2 candidate's route to the certificate in the order UAS.OPEN.030(2) sets

description.en: The A2 certificate is obtained by meeting four conditions in order: the A1/A3 online training and exam, practical self-training in the operating conditions of subcategory A3, a declaration of completing it, and an additional theoretical examination. Write a plan per candidate with target dates so no step is skipped or taken out of turn.

evidenceHint.en: Per-candidate A2 plan listing the four steps in order with target and completion dates

text.en: Confirm the candidate holds a valid A1/A3 proof before planning further steps.
Schedule practical self-training in A3 conditions after the A1/A3 proof.
Schedule the declaration of self-training after the training is complete.
Book the additional theory exam after the declaration.
Record target and completion dates for each step.

title.en: Run A2 practical self-training on a C2-like aircraft in A3 conditions and log it

description.en: AMC1 UAS.OPEN.030(2)(b) asks for self-training on an aircraft with the same flight characteristics, control scheme and similar weight as the one to be used, which implies a C2-labelled aircraft under 4 kg, flown in both manual and automated modes if it has both. The exercises include take-off and landing, precision manoeuvres in a given volume, hovering in all orientations and the manufacturer's contingency procedures, flown under A3 conditions.

evidenceHint.en: Self-training log per candidate naming the aircraft, site, control modes and exercises flown, with dates

text.en: Choose a C2-labelled aircraft under 4 kg similar to the one the pilot will fly in A2.
Fly the training at a site that meets the A3 conditions.
Fly take-offs, landings, precision manoeuvres and hovering in all orientations.
Practise in manual and automated modes if the aircraft has both.
Log each session with the date, site, aircraft and exercises flown.

title.en: Obtain the A2 certificate after the declaration and the additional theory exam

description.en: Once the self-training is complete the candidate declares it and sits the additional examination: at least 30 multiple-choice questions, a pass mark of 75%, covering meteorology, UAS flight performance and technical and operational mitigations for ground risk. AMC2 UAS.OPEN.030(2)(c) allows it face to face or online-proctored at the competent authority or a designated or recognised entity. File the certificate when issued.

evidenceHint.en: Declaration of self-training, exam result and A2 certificate with identification number, issuer and issue date

text.en: Submit the candidate's declaration of completing the practical self-training.
Book the additional exam at the competent authority or a designated or recognised entity.
Confirm the result shows a pass of at least 75%.
File the certificate with its identification number, issuer and issue date.
Update the roster to allow A2 assignments.

title.en: Check A2 pilots carry their certificate on every A2 flight

description.en: An A2 pilot must carry proof of competency while flying. Add a certificate-carried item to the A2 pre-flight checklist and refuse an A2 flight by a pilot who cannot show the certificate, on paper or electronically.

evidenceHint.en: A2 flight log entries confirming the certificate was carried

text.en: Add a certificate-carried item to the A2 pre-flight checklist.
Confirm the pilot can show the certificate before take-off.
Do not fly A2 if the certificate cannot be shown.
Record that the certificate was carried in the flight log.
Report a lost certificate to the training lead the same day.

title.en: Review A2 certificate files and assignments each quarter

description.en: Each quarter, check every A2 pilot's file still shows the four steps in order, that the certificate was valid on every date they flew A2, and that no A2 job was assigned to a pilot without one. Raise findings and correct rostering.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly A2 certificate review sheet with files checked, validity on flight dates and findings

text.en: List every pilot who flew A2 in the quarter.
Confirm each file shows the four steps completed in order.
Check each certificate was valid on every date the pilot flew A2.
Search rostering for A2 assignments to pilots without a certificate.
Raise findings and correct rostering where gaps are found.

templates.title: Class C2 aircraft configured for subcategory A2
templates.description: Only a class C2 aircraft that still complies with its class flies in subcategory A2, with active and updated remote ID and geo-awareness and a working low-speed mode, and no legacy or privately built aircraft is ever assigned to A2.
templates.objective: To ensure every A2 flight uses a conforming class C2 aircraft whose low-speed mode, remote ID and geo-awareness are verified before it is released to A2 work.
templates.successCriteria:
Every aircraft used for A2 work carries a C2 label and has a declaration of conformity naming class C2.
Every A2 aircraft has a release record showing its low-speed mode limits ground speed to 3 m/s and its height limiter works.
Every A2 flight log records remote ID and geo-awareness active and the take-off mass under 4 kg including payload.
No A2 flight in the period used a legacy, privately built or non-C2 aircraft.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the fleet register entries, declarations of conformity and label photographs for aircraft used in A2.
Obtain the A2 release records with low-speed mode and height limiter checks.
Obtain A2 flight logs with aircraft, payload and the remote ID and geo-awareness checks.
Obtain the firmware update history for each A2 aircraft.

Analysis:
Reconcile every aircraft named in sampled A2 flight logs with a C2 declaration and label on file.
Read each release record for a low-speed mode test showing ground speed held at 3 m/s or less, and a height limiter test.
Compare the take-off mass recorded with payload in sampled logs with the 4 kg limit.
Check sampled logs for remote ID and geo-awareness confirmed active.
Compare the firmware history with the release tests and find updates not followed by a new test.

Output:
Any A2 flight by an aircraft without a C2 declaration and label.
A list of A2 aircraft without a release test of low-speed mode or height limiter.
Any A2 flight at 4 kg or more, or without remote ID and geo-awareness confirmed.

title.en: Identify the class C2 aircraft eligible for A2 work and exclude every other aircraft

description.en: UAS.OPEN.030(3) admits only an aircraft marked as class C2 and complying with that class. Mark in the fleet register which aircraft carry a C2 label and a matching declaration, and mark every legacy, privately built or other-class aircraft as never eligible for A2.

evidenceHint.en: Fleet register extract marking each aircraft eligible or not eligible for A2, with the C2 evidence for each eligible one

text.en: List every aircraft in the fleet with its class label.
Mark aircraft with a C2 label and a declaration naming C2 as eligible for A2.
Mark legacy and privately built aircraft as not eligible for A2.
Mark aircraft of any other class as not eligible for A2.
Date the extract and update it when the fleet changes.

title.en: Test low-speed mode and the height limiter before releasing a C2 aircraft to A2 work

description.en: A C2 must have a low-speed mode that limits ground speed to no more than 3 m/s and a height-limiting function, and the A2 distance rules depend on the first. Before an aircraft first goes into A2 service, and after any firmware update, fly a short test that shows low-speed mode holds ground speed at 3 m/s or less and that the height limiter stops the climb at the set value.

evidenceHint.en: Release test record per C2 aircraft with measured ground speed in low-speed mode and height limiter result

text.en: Activate low-speed mode and fly a straight line at full control input.
Read the ground speed from telemetry and confirm it stays at 3 m/s or below.
Set the height limiter to a test value and climb to confirm it stops there.
Record the results and the firmware version tested.
Repeat the test after every firmware update.

title.en: Confirm C2 configuration, mass and remote ID before each A2 flight

description.en: Before each A2 flight the pilot confirms the aircraft is a released C2, its take-off mass with payload is under the 4 kg C2 limit, low-speed mode is available, and remote ID and geo-awareness are active and updated as UAS.OPEN.030(3) requires. Record these in the flight log.

evidenceHint.en: A2 flight log entries with aircraft identity, take-off mass, low-speed mode availability and remote ID and geo-awareness checks

text.en: Confirm the aircraft is marked eligible and released for A2 in the register.
Confirm the take-off mass with payload is under 4 kg.
Confirm low-speed mode can be switched on from the controller.
Confirm remote ID and geo-awareness are active and updated.
Record the checks in the flight log before take-off.

title.en: Withdraw a C2 aircraft from A2 work when its class conformity is in doubt

description.en: A failed low-speed mode test, a missing label, a non-allowed payload or a repair outside the manufacturer's instructions puts the aircraft's C2 status in doubt. Withdraw it from A2 work at once and pass it to the change assessment, returning it only when it is released again.

evidenceHint.en: Withdrawal record per aircraft with the reason, the date and the later release or conformity-lost decision

text.en: Mark the aircraft not available for A2 as soon as a doubt is raised.
Record the reason, such as a failed test, missing label or unapproved change.
Pass the aircraft to the change assessment for a decision.
Return it to A2 work only after a new release test.
Tell the flight planners of the withdrawal and the return.

title.en: Inspect a sample of A2 aircraft and logs each quarter for C2 conformity

description.en: Each quarter, inspect a sample of A2 aircraft for label and configuration and compare a sample of A2 flight logs with the register: every aircraft used was a released C2, under 4 kg, with low-speed mode, remote ID and geo-awareness confirmed. Raise findings for any gap.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly A2 conformity inspection sheet with aircraft and logs sampled and findings raised

text.en: Select a sample of A2 aircraft and inspect each label and configuration.
Select a sample of A2 flight logs from the quarter.
Confirm each logged aircraft was a released C2 at the time.
Check each logged take-off mass was under 4 kg.
Raise a finding for each gap and file the sheet.

templates.title: Operating areas selected for subcategory A3
templates.description: A3 flights take place only where the pilot reasonably expects no uninvolved person to be endangered for the whole operation and at least 150 m from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas, and are adjusted or stopped if someone enters.
templates.objective: To ensure every A3 site is surveyed against the 150 m and no-endangerment conditions before use, and that pilots react correctly when an uninvolved person comes within range.
templates.successCriteria:
Every A3 site used in the period has a dated site survey and map with the 150 m buffer from residential, commercial, industrial and recreational areas drawn.
No A3 track enters the 150 m buffer of its site map.
Every A3 flight log records whether an uninvolved person entered the range and what the pilot did.
Whenever a person entered, the distance kept met the largest of 30 m, the height and 2 seconds at maximum speed, or the flight was stopped.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the A3 site surveys and maps with the 150 m buffers drawn.
Obtain A3 flight plans, flight logs and tracks for the period.
Obtain incident reports for A3 operations.
Obtain the re-survey records for each A3 site.

Analysis:
Compare a sample of A3 sites with current maps or aerial imagery for residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas within 150 m that the survey missed.
Overlay sampled tracks on the site maps and look for entries into the buffer.
For each logged entry of an uninvolved person, compute the minimum distance kept from the track and compare it with the largest of 30 m, the height and 2 seconds at the aircraft's maximum speed, as AMC1 UAS.OPEN.040(1) estimates.
Compare incident reports with the logs for encounters not recorded.
Check each site was re-surveyed within the year and after any reported change in land use nearby.

Output:
A list of A3 sites whose survey missed an area within 150 m.
Any A3 track that entered its buffer.
Any encounter with an uninvolved person where the distance kept fell short or no action was recorded.

title.en: Map each A3 site and its 150 m buffer from residential, commercial, industrial and recreational areas

description.en: UAS.OPEN.040(2) keeps A3 flights at least 150 m horizontally from residential, commercial, industrial or recreational areas. Before a site is used, survey it on current maps or imagery and on the ground, mark every such area nearby and draw the 150 m buffer, so the flyable area is visible to the pilot and to a reviewer.

evidenceHint.en: A3 site survey and map per site with nearby areas marked and the 150 m buffer drawn, dated and signed

text.en: Review current maps and aerial imagery of the site and its surroundings.
Mark every residential, commercial, industrial or recreational area nearby.
Draw a 150 m buffer from each marked area and shade the flyable area.
Walk the site to confirm the map and note paths, roads and access points.
Date and sign the survey and file it under the site name.

title.en: Plan each A3 flight inside the surveyed area where no uninvolved person is expected

description.en: UAS.OPEN.040(1) requires the pilot to reasonably expect that no uninvolved person will be endangered within the range where the aircraft is flown for the entire operation. Use the site survey to plan the flight path and any geofence inside the flyable area, and note how people could reach the area, such as footpaths, and how they will be watched for.

evidenceHint.en: A3 flight plans referencing the site survey, the planned path inside the flyable area and the watch for people

text.en: Open the site survey and confirm it is current for the job.
Plan the flight path inside the flyable area away from the buffer.
Set a geofence or flight boundary where the aircraft supports one.
Note the paths or access points from which people could arrive.
Assign an observer to watch those points when one is available.

title.en: Reposition or stop an A3 flight when an uninvolved person enters its range

description.en: AMC1 UAS.OPEN.040(1) says that if an uninvolved person enters the range, the pilot adjusts the operation to keep them safe and stops if safety cannot be ensured, and estimates the minimum distance from a passer-by as the largest of 30 m, the flying height and the distance the aircraft covers in 2 seconds at maximum speed. Make this the trained response and record each occurrence.

evidenceHint.en: A3 flight log entries for each person entering the range, with distance kept, action taken and time

text.en: Work out the minimum distance for the flight from 30 m, the height and 2 seconds at maximum speed.
Move the aircraft to keep at least that distance as soon as a person enters.
Stop the flight and land safely if the distance cannot be kept.
Resume only when the person has left the range.
Record the time, distance kept and action in the flight log.

title.en: Re-check A3 site maps when land use around them changes, and at least yearly

description.en: Sites change: a car park becomes a playground, a field becomes a building site. Re-check each A3 site's map every year and whenever the operator learns of a change nearby, and withdraw the site until the new survey is done if an area now sits within 150 m of the flyable area.

evidenceHint.en: Re-survey records per A3 site with date, changes found and withdrawal or re-approval

text.en: List the A3 sites due for re-survey this year.
Compare each site with current maps and imagery for new areas nearby.
Withdraw a site at once if a new area falls within 150 m of the flyable area.
Redraw the buffer and re-approve the site when the survey is updated.
Record the re-survey and its outcome.

title.en: Sample A3 tracks and encounters each month against site maps and distance rules

description.en: Each month, overlay a sample of A3 tracks on their site maps and check none entered a buffer, and read every logged encounter with an uninvolved person for the distance kept and the action taken. Raise findings and re-train pilots where the response fell short.

evidenceHint.en: Monthly A3 sample worksheet with tracks overlaid, buffer entries, encounters checked and findings

text.en: Select a sample of the month's A3 flights across sites and pilots.
Overlay each track on its site map and look for buffer entries.
Read each logged encounter for the distance kept and the action taken.
Compare the distance with the largest of 30 m, the height and 2 seconds at maximum speed.
Raise findings and arrange re-training where needed.

templates.title: Aircraft eligible for subcategory A3
templates.description: Only aircraft that UAS.OPEN.040(4) or Article 20(b) admit fly in subcategory A3: privately built under 25 kg, legacy under 25 kg placed on the market before 1 January 2024, class C2 or C3 with remote ID and geo-awareness active, or class C4.
templates.objective: To ensure every aircraft assigned to A3 work holds one of the bases A3 admits, stays under 25 kg with its payload and flies with the functions its class requires.
templates.successCriteria:
Every aircraft assigned to A3 work in the period has an A3 eligibility basis recorded in the fleet register.
Every privately built or Article 20(b) aircraft has a recorded MTOM including payload under 25 kg.
Every Article 20(b) aircraft has evidence it was placed on the market before 1 January 2024.
Every A3 flight with a C2 or C3 records remote ID and geo-awareness active and updated.
No aircraft without an A3 basis was offered to an A3 job in planning during the period.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the fleet register with each aircraft's A3 eligibility basis and mass figures.
Obtain market-date evidence for Article 20(b) aircraft and declarations for class aircraft.
Obtain A3 job assignments and flight logs for the period.
Obtain the weighing records in heaviest configuration for privately built and legacy aircraft.

Analysis:
Trace each aircraft used for A3 work to an eligibility basis recorded before it flew.
Compare the weighed MTOM with payload of privately built and legacy aircraft with 25 kg.
Check the market-date evidence of each Article 20(b) aircraft.
For sampled C2 and C3 flights, confirm the log records remote ID and geo-awareness active and updated.
Check class aircraft against their declarations of conformity for the class recorded.
Search planning records for A3 jobs that offered an aircraft with no A3 basis.

Output:
A list of aircraft that flew A3 without an eligibility basis.
Any privately built or legacy aircraft at or over 25 kg with its payload.
Any C2 or C3 A3 flight without remote ID and geo-awareness confirmed.

title.en: Map each fleet aircraft to an A3 eligibility basis or mark it not eligible for A3

description.en: UAS.OPEN.040(4) admits a privately built aircraft under 25 kg, an Article 20(b) aircraft (a non-class aircraft under 25 kg placed on the market before 1 January 2024), a class C2 or C3 flown with active and updated remote ID and geo-awareness, and a class C4. Record the basis each aircraft holds, or that it holds none, so A3 planning draws only on eligible aircraft.

evidenceHint.en: Fleet register column showing the A3 basis per aircraft, or not eligible, with the date it was set

text.en: List every aircraft the operator might use for A3 work.
Record class C2, C3 or C4 from the class label and declaration of conformity.
Record privately built aircraft under 25 kg as their own basis.
Record legacy aircraft under 25 kg placed on the market before 1 January 2024 under Article 20(b).
Mark every other aircraft as not eligible for A3.

title.en: Record the take-off mass and market-date evidence of privately built and legacy A3 aircraft

description.en: The privately built and Article 20(b) bases rest on a take-off mass under 25 kg including payload, and for legacy aircraft on being placed on the market before 1 January 2024. Weigh each in its heaviest flying configuration and keep the purchase or market-date evidence on its record.

evidenceHint.en: Weighing record in heaviest configuration and market-date evidence per privately built or legacy A3 aircraft

text.en: Weigh each aircraft with its heaviest battery and payload fitted.
Confirm the mass is under 25 kg and record it.
Keep the purchase or market-date evidence for each legacy aircraft.
Mark the aircraft not eligible for A3 if a figure misses the limit.
Re-weigh after any change to the airframe, battery or payload.

title.en: Restrict A3 job assignment to aircraft with an A3 eligibility basis

description.en: Make the register drive A3 planning: only aircraft with an A3 basis recorded can be assigned, a C2 or C3 only while its remote ID and geo-awareness work, and every A3 flight plan names the aircraft and its basis.

evidenceHint.en: A3 flight plans naming the aircraft and its eligibility basis, and the planning rule that enforces it

text.en: Filter the aircraft offered for A3 jobs to those with an A3 basis recorded.
Exclude any C2 or C3 whose remote ID or geo-awareness is reported faulty.
Record the aircraft and its basis in each A3 flight plan.
Refuse a planned A3 job if no eligible aircraft is available.
Review the filter whenever the fleet register changes.

title.en: Confirm remote ID and geo-awareness before each A3 flight of a C2 or C3 aircraft

description.en: A C2 or C3 flown in A3 must have remote ID and geo-awareness active and updated, just as in A2. A class C4 and the privately built and legacy bases carry no such condition. Add the check to the A3 checklist for C2 and C3 aircraft only, and record it.

evidenceHint.en: A3 flight log entries for C2 and C3 aircraft recording remote ID and geo-awareness confirmed active and updated

text.en: Check the aircraft's class in the register before the flight.
For a C2 or C3, confirm geo-awareness is loaded with current zone data.
For a C2 or C3, confirm remote ID is active and carries the operator number.
Ground a C2 or C3 whose remote ID shows an error.
Record the checks in the flight log.

title.en: Reconcile A3 flights with the fleet register's eligibility bases each quarter

description.en: Each quarter, take the A3 flights flown and check every aircraft used held an A3 basis, that privately built and legacy aircraft stayed under 25 kg, and that C2 and C3 flights recorded remote ID and geo-awareness. Raise findings and correct the register.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly A3 reconciliation listing aircraft used, bases held, mass checks and findings

text.en: List every aircraft used for A3 flights in the quarter.
Confirm each held an A3 basis on the dates it flew.
Spot-check the mass of a sample of privately built and legacy aircraft.
Check C2 and C3 flight logs for the remote ID and geo-awareness entries.
Raise findings and correct the register where it is wrong.

templates.title: Remote pilot competency for subcategory A3
templates.description: Every A3 pilot knows the manufacturer's instructions and has completed the online training and passed the online theoretical examination, whatever the aircraft; A3 is also where an A2 candidate flies their practical self-training.
templates.objective: To ensure no pilot flies in A3 without the online training and exam passed and the proof carried, including A2 candidates doing their self-training there.
templates.successCriteria:
Every pilot who flew in A3 holds a valid A1/A3 proof from the competent authority or its designated entity.
Every A3 pilot has a familiarisation record for each model they fly.
Every A3 flight log confirms the proof was carried.
Every A2 candidate's self-training flights in A3 were flown by a pilot already holding the A1/A3 proof.
No pilot without an A1/A3 proof on file was assigned to an A3 job in the period, whatever the aircraft class.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the roster of pilots who flew A3, with their A1/A3 proofs and familiarisation records.
Obtain A3 flight logs for the period, including A2 self-training flights.
Obtain the rostering records for A3 jobs in the period.

Analysis:
For each sampled A3 flight, check the pilot held a valid A1/A3 proof on the flight date and the log confirms it was carried.
Check each pilot's familiarisation record covers the model flown.
For each A2 candidate's self-training flight, compare its date with the date of the candidate's A1/A3 proof.
Compare each proof's issuer with the competent authorities and designated entities of the Member States.
Search rostering for A3 assignments to pilots without a proof on file.
Check each proof was inside its five-year validity on every date its holder flew A3.

Output:
Any A3 flight by a pilot without a valid A1/A3 proof or without it carried.
A list of pilots without familiarisation for a model they flew.
Any A2 self-training flight made before the candidate held the A1/A3 proof.

title.en: Restrict A3 rostering to pilots who hold the A1/A3 online proof

description.en: UAS.OPEN.040(3) requires every A3 pilot, whatever the aircraft, to be familiar with the manufacturer's instructions and to have completed the online training course and passed the online theoretical examination referred to in UAS.OPEN.020(4)(b). Unlike A1, there is no class of aircraft that exempts an A3 pilot from it. Set the roster so no pilot can be assigned to A3 without the proof on file.

evidenceHint.en: Roster rule and extract showing every A3-rostered pilot with an A1/A3 proof on file

text.en: List every pilot who may be rostered for A3 work.
Check each has an A1/A3 proof of completion on file.
Set the roster so a pilot without the proof cannot be assigned to A3.
Note that no aircraft class exempts an A3 pilot from the exam.
Date the extract and update it as pilots join.

title.en: Obtain and file the A1/A3 online proof for each new A3 pilot

description.en: The online exam is set by the competent authority or its designated entity: 40 multiple-choice questions with a pass mark of 75%, across the nine subjects of UAS.OPEN.020(4)(b), including privacy and data protection, insurance and security. Have each new A3 pilot complete the course and pass the exam, then file the proof with its identification number and issue date for validity tracking.

evidenceHint.en: A1/A3 proof per A3 pilot with identification number, issuer and issue date, filed on the roster

text.en: Direct the pilot to the competent authority's online course and exam.
Have the pilot complete the course and pass the exam.
File the proof with its identification number and issuer.
Record the issue date on the roster for validity tracking.
Allow A3 assignments only once the proof is filed.

title.en: Train each A3 pilot on the manufacturer's instructions for the heavier models flown in A3

description.en: A3 is where the operator flies its larger aircraft, such as C3, C4 or privately built ones up to 25 kg, whose limits, payload rules and lost-link behaviour differ from smaller models. Walk each A3 pilot through the instructions for every model they will fly there and record it before their first A3 flight on that model.

evidenceHint.en: Familiarisation record per A3 pilot and model with topics, date and trainer

text.en: Give the pilot the manufacturer's instructions for each A3 model.
Cover the weather limits, payload rules and lost-link behaviour.
Practise the model's emergency and return functions in a safe area.
Record the familiarisation with the model, date and trainer.
Repeat it when the manufacturer revises the instructions.

title.en: Confirm A2 candidates hold the A1/A3 proof before their self-training flights in A3

description.en: The A2 certificate requires practical self-training in the operating conditions of subcategory A3, after the A1/A3 online exam. So every self-training flight is an A3 flight, and the candidate must already hold the A1/A3 proof and fly to the A3 conditions. Check the proof before the first self-training flight and log those flights as A3.

evidenceHint.en: A3 flight logs of A2 self-training flights with the candidate's A1/A3 proof date recorded before the first flight

text.en: Check the A2 candidate's A1/A3 proof is on file before self-training starts.
Plan the self-training at a site that meets the A3 conditions.
Log each self-training flight as an A3 flight.
Confirm the candidate carries the A1/A3 proof on each flight.
Keep the logs with the candidate's A2 file.

title.en: Review A3 pilot proofs and A2 self-training flights each quarter

description.en: Each quarter, sample A3 flights and check the pilot held a valid A1/A3 proof and carried it, was familiarised with the model, and that every A2 self-training flight was made after the candidate's A1/A3 proof. Raise findings and correct rostering.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly A3 competency review sheet with flights sampled, proof and familiarisation checks and findings

text.en: Select a sample of A3 flights from the quarter, including self-training flights.
Check each pilot's A1/A3 proof was valid on the flight date and carried.
Check each pilot's familiarisation record covers the model flown.
Compare each self-training flight date with the candidate's proof date.
Raise findings and correct rostering where gaps are found.

templates.title: Specific-category procedures, limitations and mitigation review
templates.description: Every specific-category operation runs on a stated basis, a declaration, an operational authorisation or the operator's LUC, under written procedures and limitations adapted to it, and the operator regularly evaluates whether its mitigations still work and updates them.
templates.objective: To ensure each specific-category operation is flown on a stated basis, under procedures adapted to its risk and within its limits, with mitigations the operator re-evaluates.
templates.successCriteria:
Every specific-category operation in the period names its basis: a declaration with its confirmation of receipt, an operational authorisation, or the LUC privilege it is flown under.
Written procedures cover operational safety, nuisance to people and animals and radio spectrum use, and say which operation types each applies to.
Flight records show every sampled operation flown inside the limitations, conditions and mitigations of its declaration or authorisation.
A dated mitigation review, held at least yearly and after each occurrence or change, records what was found and updated.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of specific-category operation types with the declaration, authorisation or LUC terms each relies on.
Obtain the operator's specific-category procedures, nuisance guidelines and spectrum rules, with versions and approval dates.
Obtain flight records for the period and the declarations or authorisations they were flown under.
Obtain the mitigation reviews held in the period and the occurrence reports raised.

Analysis:
Trace a sample of flights to an operation type in the register and confirm the basis named was valid on the flight date.
Compare each sampled flight's height, area, time, aircraft and crew with the limitations and conditions of its basis.
Read the procedures against UAS.SPEC.050(1)(a): safety procedures and nuisance guidelines, with data protection and security covered by the controls that own them.
Check that each mitigation review followed its trigger, judged every mitigation and recorded what changed.
Confirm that a change to the mitigations was notified, or an updated authorisation sought, before the changed operation flew.

Output:
A list of sampled flights with no valid basis or flown outside its limits.
A statement of which procedure areas are written and which are missing.
A list of mitigation reviews that were overdue, incomplete or not acted on.

title.en: Map each specific-category operation type to the declaration, authorisation or LUC privilege it relies on

description.en: Article 5 and UAS.SPEC.010 give a specific-category operation three possible bases: a declaration against a standard scenario, an operational authorisation backed by a risk assessment, or the privileges of a light UAS operator certificate. List every type of specific-category work the operator does or plans, name the basis each one relies on and the document that proves it, and mark any type that has none so it is not flown.

evidenceHint.en: Register of specific-category operation types, each with its basis (declaration, authorisation or LUC), the document reference and its validity date

text.en: List every type of specific-category work the operator flies or plans to fly.
Name the basis for each type: a declaration, an operational authorisation or an LUC privilege.
Record the reference and validity date of the document that grants each basis.
Mark any operation type without a basis as not to be flown and tell the planners.
Date the register and name the person who keeps it up to date.

title.en: Write the specific-category operating procedures and the nuisance guidelines for remote pilots

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(a) asks for procedures and limitations adapted to the operation and its risk, including procedures that keep the operation safe and guidelines that help remote pilots plan flights to minimise noise and other emission-related nuisance to people and animals. Write them for each operation type, and point to the data-protection procedure and the security procedure kept under their own controls rather than repeating them.

evidenceHint.en: Approved procedure set for specific-category operations with safety procedures, nuisance guidelines and references to the data-protection and security procedures

text.en: Write the safety procedures for each operation type, from planning to post-flight.
State the operating limitations each procedure enforces, such as height, area and weather.
Add guidelines on routes, timing and heights that reduce noise and disturbance to people and animals.
Reference the data-protection procedure and the security procedure instead of copying them.
Approve the procedure set and record its version and approval date.

title.en: Set radio spectrum rules for the aircraft and ground equipment used in specific operations

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(c) requires every operation to use radio spectrum efficiently and avoid harmful interference. Record the command and control and payload links each aircraft uses, forbid changes to frequency or transmit power that the manufacturer does not provide for, and give pilots a way to report interference they cause or meet, so a spectrum problem is handled before it becomes a safety one.

evidenceHint.en: Spectrum rule in the procedures, a list of the links each aircraft uses, and the interference reporting route

text.en: List the command and control and payload links each aircraft and ground station uses.
Forbid frequency or power settings the manufacturer's instructions do not provide for.
Ban third-party radio modules, amplifiers and antennas not approved by the manufacturer.
Give pilots a route to report interference caused or experienced, and record each report.

title.en: Check each specific-category flight against the limits of its declaration or authorisation

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(f) requires each operation to stay within the limitations, conditions and mitigation measures of its declaration or authorisation. Turn those limits into a pre-flight check for the operation type, have the pilot confirm them before take-off, and compare the flight record with them afterwards so any departure is caught and reported rather than repeated.

evidenceHint.en: Completed pre-flight limit checks and post-flight comparisons for the period, with each departure recorded and reported

text.en: Extract the limitations, conditions and mitigations from the declaration or authorisation.
Turn them into a pre-flight check the pilot signs before take-off.
Compare the flight record with the limits after landing and note any departure.
Report every departure to the operations manager on the day it is found.
Keep the signed check with the flight record for the period records are retained.

title.en: Evaluate whether the specific-category mitigations still work and update them

description.en: UAS.SPEC.010 requires the operator to regularly evaluate the adequacy of its mitigation measures and update them where necessary. Review every mitigation at least yearly and after any occurrence, change of aircraft, crew or area, record whether it still works, and before changing one decide whether the declaration must be updated with the authority or an updated authorisation sought first.

evidenceHint.en: Dated mitigation review record listing each mitigation, its assessment, the change decided and any notification or application it needed

text.en: Schedule a review of every mitigation at least once a year.
Add a review after each occurrence and each change of aircraft, crew or operating area.
Record for each mitigation whether it worked as intended, with the evidence relied on.
Decide whether a change needs the declaration updated or a new authorisation before it applies.
Update the procedures and tell the crews before the next affected flight.

templates.title: Competency-based training for remote pilots and essential personnel
templates.description: Remote pilots in the specific category are trained to the competencies Article 8(2) lists and to what their declaration, authorisation or LUC requires, other essential personnel complete the operator's on-the-job training, and the operator keeps a current list of the pilot designated for each flight.
templates.objective: To ensure everyone with a duty essential to a specific-category operation is trained to the competencies it needs, and that each flight has a designated, competent remote pilot.
templates.successCriteria:
A training matrix names, for every specific-category role, the training its declaration, authorisation or LUC requires and the Article 8(2) competencies it must show.
Every remote pilot on the list holds a current training record, assessed on performance, for each operation type they are designated for.
Every observer and other essential crew member has completed the operator's on-the-job training and been briefed on the operations manual where one is required.
Every sampled flight names its designated remote pilot, who carried proof of competency.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the training matrix, the remote pilot syllabus and the on-the-job training material for essential personnel.
Obtain the training and assessment records of every remote pilot and essential crew member active in the period.
Obtain the list of designated remote pilots and a sample of flight records.
Obtain the declaration, authorisation or LUC terms that set training requirements.

Analysis:
Compare the syllabus with the eight competencies of Article 8(2) and note any not trained or not assessed.
Compare the matrix with the training the declaration, authorisation or LUC requires for each role.
For authorised operations, confirm the training was given in cooperation with an entity designated by the competent authority where the authorisation requires it.
Trace each sampled flight to its designated pilot and confirm that pilot's training covered the operation type on the flight date.
Confirm each essential crew member on the sampled flights had completed on-the-job training first.

Output:
A list of Article 8(2) competencies the syllabus does not train or assess.
A list of flights flown by a pilot or crew member not trained for that operation.
A list of flights with no designated pilot recorded.

title.en: Identify the training each specific-category role needs from its authorisation, scenario or LUC

description.en: Under Article 8(2) and UAS.SPEC.050(1)(d) a specific-category remote pilot's competency is set by the operational authorisation, the standard scenario or the LUC, so the training differs by basis. Build a matrix that lists each role, including remote pilots, observers and launch and recovery crew, the operation types it works on and the training each basis requires, so no one is trained to the wrong standard.

evidenceHint.en: Training matrix listing each specific-category role, the operation types it supports and the training required by each declaration, authorisation or LUC

text.en: List every role with a duty essential to specific-category operations.
Record the operation types each role supports and the basis each type is flown under.
Copy the training each declaration, authorisation or LUC requires into the matrix.
Flag any role where two bases require different training and record which applies when.
Approve the matrix and date it.

title.en: Build a competency-based remote pilot syllabus covering the eight Article 8(2) competencies

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(d)(ii) requires remote pilot training to be competency based and to include the Article 8(2) competencies: operational procedures, aeronautical communication, flight path and automation management, leadership and teamwork, problem solving, situational awareness, workload management, and coordination or handover. Write a syllabus that trains and assesses each one by observed performance, not attendance.

evidenceHint.en: Remote pilot syllabus mapping each Article 8(2) competency to training content and a performance assessment

text.en: List the eight Article 8(2) competencies as the headings of the syllabus.
Write the training content and an observed assessment for each competency.
Include normal, contingency and emergency procedures, flight planning and pre- and post-flight inspections.
Arrange delivery with the designated entity where an operational authorisation requires it.
Align training for declared operations with the mitigations of the standard scenario.

title.en: Deliver on-the-job training to observers and other essential crew before their first operation

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(e) requires personnel in charge of duties essential to the operation, other than the remote pilot, to complete on-the-job training developed by the operator, to be informed about the operations manual where the risk assessment requires one and about the procedures, and to have current information on the geographical zones for the operation. Train and record each person before they take a role.

evidenceHint.en: On-the-job training records for each observer and essential crew member, with the date and the operations manual and procedures briefed

text.en: Write the on-the-job training for each essential role other than the remote pilot.
Brief each trainee on the operations manual where one is required, and on the procedures.
Give each trainee the geographical zone information for the operations they will support.
Record completion with the trainer's and trainee's names and the date.

title.en: Name the remote pilot for each specific-category flight and keep the pilot list current

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(b) and (j) require a remote pilot to be designated for each flight and an up-to-date list of designated pilots. For autonomous operations the operator instead allocates the pilot's pre-flight and in-flight duties to named people for every phase. Before each flight, check that the designated pilot is trained for the operation type, carries proof of competency and knows the manufacturer's instructions.

evidenceHint.en: Flight records naming the designated remote pilot, the current designated-pilot list and, for autonomous operations, the allocation of duties

text.en: Name the remote pilot for each flight in the flight plan before it is released.
For autonomous operations, allocate each pilot duty to a named person for every phase of flight.
Check the pilot's training covers the operation type and that their proof of competency is current.
Confirm the pilot knows the manufacturer's instructions for the aircraft being flown.
Update the designated-pilot list whenever a pilot is added, suspended or removed.

title.en: Assess each remote pilot against the specific-category syllabus every year

description.en: Competency fades and the operation changes. Once a year, and after an occurrence that points to a training gap, observe each remote pilot against the syllabus competencies on the operation types they fly, record the result, retrain any gap before the pilot is designated again, and update the syllabus when the authorisation, scenario or LUC changes.

evidenceHint.en: Annual assessment record per remote pilot against each syllabus competency, with retraining completed for gaps

text.en: Schedule an observed assessment for each remote pilot once a year.
Assess each competency on the operation types the pilot is designated for.
Withhold designation for any operation type where a competency gap is found until retrained.
Revise the syllabus when the authorisation, scenario or LUC terms change.

templates.title: Three-year records of personnel, maintenance and operations
templates.description: The operator keeps up-to-date records of personnel qualifications and training, of maintenance and of operations, including unusual occurrences, for at least the three years UAS.SPEC.050(1)(g) sets, in storage that survives staff turnover.
templates.objective: To ensure the records the specific category requires exist for every person, aircraft and operation, are kept for at least three years, and can be produced on request.
templates.successCriteria:
Qualification and training records exist for every remote pilot, essential crew member and maintenance staff member, and are kept at least three years after each person leaves or changes position.
Maintenance records exist for every maintenance activity and are kept at least three years.
Operations records exist for every flight, including unusual technical or operational occurrences and any data the declaration or authorisation requires, and are kept at least three years.
A retrieval test produces a record at least three years old within the time set.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the record inventory and retention rules for specific-category operations.
Obtain the list of flights flown, maintenance carried out and personnel joining, leaving or moving in the last three years.
Obtain the declarations or authorisations in force and any extra records they require.
Obtain the results of the last retrieval test.

Analysis:
Sample flights and confirm an operations record exists for each, with any unusual occurrence noted.
Sample maintenance jobs and confirm each has a maintenance record.
Sample people who left or changed position in the last three years and confirm their qualification and training records are still held.
Compare the record set with the extra data each declaration or authorisation requires.
Read the retention settings of each store and confirm none deletes a record earlier than three years.

Output:
A list of flights, maintenance jobs and people with no record.
A list of stores whose retention is shorter than three years.
The result of the retrieval test against the time set.

title.en: Inventory the records the specific category and each authorisation or declaration require

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(g) names three record classes: qualifications and training of remote pilots, essential personnel and maintenance staff; maintenance activities; and operations information, including unusual technical or operational occurrences and other data the declaration or authorisation requires. List each record, where it is kept, who writes it and the retention period that applies, adding the extra items each declaration or authorisation names.

evidenceHint.en: Record inventory listing each record type, its store, its owner and its retention period, including items each declaration or authorisation requires

text.en: List the personnel, maintenance and operations records UAS.SPEC.050(1)(g) requires.
Add every extra record each declaration or authorisation names.
Record where each one is stored and who is responsible for writing it.
Set the retention period against each record, never shorter than three years.

title.en: Set retention so personnel records outlast a person's departure by three years

description.en: The personnel clock in UAS.SPEC.050(1)(g)(i) runs from when a person leaves the organisation or changes position, not from when the record was made, so a simple age-based deletion rule loses records too early. Configure each store so personnel records are kept at least three years after departure or change of position, and maintenance and operations records at least three years, in storage that does not depend on one person's account.

evidenceHint.en: Retention configuration for each record store, showing the departure-based clock for personnel records and the three-year minimum for the others

text.en: Start the personnel retention clock at the date a person leaves or changes position.
Set maintenance and operations records to be kept for at least three years.
Move records off personal devices and accounts into storage the organisation controls.
Disable any automatic deletion that would remove a record before its retention ends.
Back up the record stores and record where the backups are kept.

title.en: Record unusual technical and operational occurrences in the operations log after each flight

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(g)(iii) requires the information on operations to include any unusual technical or operational occurrence. After every flight, have the pilot complete the operations record with the flight details and anything unusual, such as a link loss, an unexpected landing or a near miss, and link the entry to an occurrence report wherever one is filed.

evidenceHint.en: Operations log entries for the period, each with flight details and any unusual occurrence, linked to occurrence reports where filed

text.en: Complete the operations record for every flight on the day it is flown.
Note any unusual technical or operational event, even if the flight finished normally.
Add the data the declaration or authorisation requires for that operation type.
Link the entry to the occurrence report wherever one is filed.

title.en: Test that a specific-category record from three years ago can be produced on request

description.en: A record that cannot be found when an inspector asks for it serves no purpose. Pick records near the end of their three-year retention from each class, time how long it takes to produce each one from storage, and fix whatever slowed or prevented retrieval, such as an unindexed archive or a leaver's locked account.

evidenceHint.en: Retrieval test record listing each record requested, its age, the time taken to produce it and any problem fixed

text.en: Choose one personnel, one maintenance and one operations record close to three years old.
Ask someone other than the record owner to produce each one and time it.
Record any record that could not be found or took longer than the time set.
Fix the cause, such as missing indexing or access tied to a leaver, and retest.

title.en: Reconcile flights, maintenance and staff changes with the records held each quarter

description.en: Gaps show up when the records are compared with what actually happened. Each quarter, compare flights flown with operations records, maintenance done with maintenance records, and joiners, leavers and role changes with personnel records, then chase each missing record and note any repeat cause so the process that should have produced it is fixed.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly reconciliation worksheet comparing flights, maintenance and staff changes with records held, listing gaps and their closure

text.en: Compare the quarter's flights with the operations records and list any flight without one.
Compare maintenance carried out with the maintenance records and list any gap.
Compare joiners, leavers and role changes with the personnel records held.
Assign each gap an owner and a due date, and record when it is closed.

templates.title: Maintenance programme, maintenance staff and certified equipment
templates.description: Specific-category aircraft are designed so a failure keeps them in the operational volume, are maintained to defined instructions by trained, listed staff, carry a green flashing light and working remote identification, and any certified equipment is managed as UAS.SPEC.100 requires.
templates.objective: To ensure every aircraft used in the specific category is fit by design, maintained by competent staff to defined instructions, equipped as required and, where certified, kept in certified condition.
templates.successCriteria:
Every specific-category aircraft type has a recorded basis showing a possible failure will not take it outside the operational volume or cause a fatality.
Every aircraft type has maintenance instructions, and every maintenance job was done by a person on the current maintenance staff list who is trained for it.
Every aircraft in use carries at least one green flashing light and an active, up-to-date remote identification system.
Where certified equipment or a certificated aircraft is used, service time is recorded and every applicable airworthiness directive and mandated safety measure is applied.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the design basis recorded for each specific-category aircraft type and the manufacturer's documentation it relies on.
Obtain the maintenance instructions, the maintenance staff list and their training records.
Obtain the maintenance records and the pre-flight equipment checks for the period.
Obtain the register of certified equipment and certificated aircraft, service time records and the airworthiness directives and safety information that apply.

Analysis:
Read each design basis for how a failure is kept inside the operational volume and how the interface limits pilot error and fatigue.
Sample maintenance jobs and confirm each followed the instructions and was signed by a listed, trained person.
Sample flights and confirm the green flashing light and remote identification were checked as working.
For certified equipment, compare service time with its limits and confirm each applicable directive and mandated measure was applied.

Output:
A list of aircraft types with no recorded design basis.
A list of maintenance jobs done outside the instructions or by unlisted staff.
A list of equipment or directive gaps found, with their owners.

title.en: Record why each specific-category aircraft type stays inside the operational volume after a failure

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(h) requires aircraft designed so a possible failure will not lead them outside the operational volume or cause a fatality, with interfaces that minimise pilot error and do not cause unreasonable fatigue, and point (i)(iii) asks for aircraft designed to minimise noise and emissions where those are of concern. For each type, record the features and documentation that show this before it is used.

evidenceHint.en: Design basis record per aircraft type citing the manufacturer's documentation for failure containment, interface design and noise

text.en: List each aircraft type used or planned for specific-category work.
Record the features that keep it in the volume after a failure, such as geofencing or flight termination.
Note how the remote station's interface limits pilot error and fatigue on long tasks.
Note whether its noise and emissions suit the areas where it will fly.
Approve the type for specific-category use only once the record is complete.

title.en: Define maintenance instructions per aircraft type and list the trained maintenance staff

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(i) and (k) require maintenance instructions, adequately trained and qualified maintenance staff and an up-to-date list of the staff the operator employs for maintenance. Write the instructions for each aircraft type from the manufacturer's documentation, set the training each task needs, and list who may carry out each task.

evidenceHint.en: Maintenance instructions per aircraft type and the current maintenance staff list with each person's training and authorised tasks

text.en: Write maintenance instructions for each aircraft type from the manufacturer's documentation.
Set the training or qualification each maintenance task needs.
List each maintenance staff member with the tasks they are authorised to carry out.
Update the list the same day someone joins, leaves or gains a qualification.

title.en: Verify the green flashing light and active remote identification on every specific-category aircraft

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(l) requires each individual aircraft to have at least one green flashing light, for visibility at night, and an active, up-to-date remote identification system. Check both when an aircraft is accepted into specific-category service, after every repair or software update, and in the pre-flight check, and withdraw an aircraft that fails either.

evidenceHint.en: Acceptance and pre-flight records showing the green flashing light and remote identification checked on each aircraft

text.en: Check the green flashing light works before an aircraft enters specific-category service.
Confirm the remote identification is active and carries the operator's current registration number.
Repeat both checks after any repair, part change or software update.
Add both items to the pre-flight check and withdraw any aircraft that fails one.

title.en: Track service time, airworthiness directives and safety information for certified equipment

description.en: UAS.SPEC.100 applies when certified equipment or a certificated aircraft is used. A certificated aircraft must comply with Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1107. Certified equipment on an aircraft without a certificate needs its service time recorded, the equipment certificate's instructions and EASA airworthiness directives followed, safety measures the competent authority mandates applied, and EASA's mandatory safety information used.

evidenceHint.en: Register of certified equipment and certificated aircraft with service time, applicable directives and their status, or a dated record that none is used

text.en: List any certified equipment fitted and any aircraft holding a certificate of airworthiness.
Record operation or service time as the equipment's instructions or procedures require.
Check EASA airworthiness directives and mandatory safety information and apply each one that applies.
Apply any safety measure the competent authority mandates and record when it was done.
Where none is used, record that UAS.SPEC.100 does not apply and re-check when the fleet changes.

title.en: Review maintenance compliance and the maintenance staff list each quarter

description.en: Sample the quarter's maintenance jobs and check each one followed its instructions and was done by a listed person trained for it. Compare the staff list with the people who actually signed for maintenance, and look for repeat defects that suggest the instructions or the training need changing.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly maintenance review listing jobs sampled, compliance with instructions, signers checked against the staff list and actions raised

text.en: Sample at least five maintenance jobs from the quarter across different aircraft.
Check each job against its instructions and the signer against the staff list.
Look for defects that recur on the same aircraft type or component.
Raise an action to change instructions or training wherever a pattern appears.

templates.title: Remote pilot duties before and during specific-category flights
templates.description: Before and during every specific-category flight the remote pilot carries out the duties UAS.SPEC.060 sets: fit to fly, zone information current, environment and aircraft checked, the right people told, and the flight kept within its limits or stopped.
templates.objective: To ensure every specific-category remote pilot is fit, prepared and compliant with their duties before each flight, and stops a flight that becomes unsafe or leaves its limits.
templates.successCriteria:
Every sampled flight has a completed pre-flight checklist covering zone information, the operating environment against the declared or authorised limits, aircraft condition and remote identification.
Every flight that required it shows the air traffic service unit, other airspace users or stakeholders were informed beforehand.
Every pilot recorded fitness to fly before duty, and no flight was flown by a pilot who declared themselves unfit.
Every discontinued flight and every flight near an emergency response is recorded with the reason or the permission held.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the specific-category pre-flight checklist and the fitness declaration used by remote pilots.
Obtain completed checklists, fitness declarations and flight records for the period.
Obtain the notifications made to air traffic service units, other airspace users and stakeholders, and the conditions requiring them.
Obtain records of discontinued flights and any permissions to fly near an emergency response.

Analysis:
Read the checklist against UAS.SPEC.060(2) and note any duty it omits.
Sample flights and confirm a completed checklist and fitness declaration exist for each, dated before take-off.
For sampled flights in areas whose authorisation or zone requires notification, confirm it was made before the flight.
Compare sampled flight tracks with the authorised or declared limits and the geographical zone limits.
Read discontinued flights for the reason and confirm the pilot acted as the procedure requires.

Output:
A list of SPEC.060 duties missing from the checklist.
A list of sampled flights with no checklist, no fitness declaration or no required notification.
A list of flights that left their limits without being discontinued.

title.en: Write the specific-category pre-flight checklist from the UAS.SPEC.060(2) duties

description.en: UAS.SPEC.060(2) sets four duties before each flight: get current information on the geographical zones, ensure the operating environment fits the authorised or declared limits and conditions, ensure the aircraft is safe to complete the flight and its remote identification is active and up to date, and ensure information about the operation has reached the air traffic service unit, other airspace users and stakeholders where required.

evidenceHint.en: Approved specific-category pre-flight checklist covering each UAS.SPEC.060(2) duty, with its version and approval date

text.en: Add a check that zone information for the area was obtained on the day of the flight.
Add a check of wind, visibility and surroundings against the authorised or declared limits.
Add the aircraft condition check and confirmation that remote identification is active and current.
Add a check that every notification the authorisation or zone requires was made.
Approve the checklist and make it part of each flight record.

title.en: Confirm each remote pilot is fit to fly before a specific-category duty

description.en: UAS.SPEC.060(1)(a) forbids a remote pilot from performing duties under the influence of psychoactive substances or alcohol, or when unfit because of injury, fatigue, medication, sickness or another cause. Have each pilot declare fitness before duty, make clear that declaring themselves unfit carries no penalty, and replace or stand down a pilot who is not fit.

evidenceHint.en: Fitness declarations signed by each remote pilot before duty, and records of any stand-down

text.en: Ask the pilot to declare before duty that they are free of alcohol, drugs, fatigue and illness.
Ask about any medication taken that could affect alertness or judgement.
Stand the pilot down without penalty if they declare themselves unfit.
Record the declaration or stand-down with the flight record.

title.en: Notify the air traffic service unit and stakeholders before flights that require it

description.en: UAS.SPEC.060(2)(d) requires the pilot to ensure that information about the operation has been made available to the relevant air traffic service unit, other airspace users and stakeholders, as the operational authorisation or the Member State's conditions for the geographical zone require. Work out who must be told for each flight, notify them in the form required, and keep the proof.

evidenceHint.en: Record of each notification made before a flight, with recipient, time and content, matched to the condition requiring it

text.en: Read the authorisation and zone conditions for who must be told about the flight.
Send the notification in the form and with the notice period the condition sets.
Keep the acknowledgement or a record of the call with the time and the person spoken to.
Delay the flight until every required notification has been made.

title.en: Halt a specific-category flight that puts aircraft, people or property at risk

description.en: During flight UAS.SPEC.060(3) requires the pilot to keep to the limits and conditions, avoid any risk of collision with manned aircraft, discontinue a flight whose continuation may pose a risk to other aircraft, people, animals, the environment or property, keep to zone limits and the operator's procedures, and stay away from an emergency response unless permitted. Record every discontinuation and its reason.

evidenceHint.en: Flight records of each discontinued flight with its reason, and any permission held to fly near an emergency response

text.en: Give way to manned aircraft and land or move away when one approaches the operating area.
Stop the flight when continuing would put aircraft, people, animals or property at risk.
Keep clear of any emergency response unless the responding services have given permission.
Record each discontinuation with the time, the reason and what was done.

title.en: Sample specific-category flight records against the remote pilot duties each month

description.en: Pick a sample of the month's specific-category flights and check that each had a fitness declaration and a completed pre-flight checklist before take-off, that required notifications were made, and that the track stayed within the authorised or declared limits and zone limits. Raise a finding for each breach and follow it to closure.

evidenceHint.en: Monthly sample worksheet listing flights reviewed, duties checked, breaches found and findings raised

text.en: Select at least five specific-category flights from the month across different pilots.
Check each for a fitness declaration and a checklist completed before take-off.
Confirm the notifications its authorisation or zone required were made.
Compare the track with the authorised or declared limits and the zone limits.
Raise a finding for each breach with an owner and a due date.

templates.title: Operations in another Member State
templates.description: Before a specific-category operation takes place partly or wholly in another Member State, the operator gives that State's competent authority what Article 13 requires for its basis, and an authorised operation waits for that authority to confirm the updated mitigations.
templates.objective: To ensure no specific-category operation is flown in another Member State until its competent authority holds what Article 13 requires and, where authorised, has confirmed the mitigations.
templates.successCriteria:
Every specific-category operation planned outside the Member State of registration is listed with its basis and the competent authority of the State of operation.
Every authorised operation abroad has an application with a copy of the authorisation, the locations and updated mitigations, and a confirmation received before the first flight.
Every declared operation abroad shows a copy of the declaration and its confirmation of receipt and completeness sent to that State's authority.
Every LUC operation abroad shows the terms of approval and the locations sent.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the list of specific-category operations flown or planned outside the Member State of registration in the period.
Obtain each Article 13 submission, the documents sent with it and the reply of the State of operation.
Obtain the flight records for those operations and the updated authorisation where the State of registration recorded the mitigations.
Obtain the national requirements matrix entry used for each destination.

Analysis:
Compare the flight records with the list to find operations abroad that were not listed.
For each authorised operation, confirm the application carried a copy of the authorisation, the locations and updated mitigations for local airspace, terrain, population and climate.
Confirm the first flight abroad took place only after the State of operation confirmed the updated mitigations.
For declared operations, confirm copies of the declaration and its confirmation were sent; for LUC operations, the terms of approval and locations.
Confirm the destination's national requirements were checked before the operation.

Output:
A list of operations abroad flown without the Article 13 submission their basis needs.
A list of authorised operations flown before confirmation.
A list of destinations where national requirements were not checked.

title.en: Identify planned specific-category operations outside the Member State of registration

description.en: Article 13 applies to any specific-category operation taking place partly or entirely in the airspace of a Member State other than the one where the operator is registered. Find each such job at the planning stage, including work close to a border whose volume or buffer crosses it, and record its basis and the competent authority of the State of intended operation.

evidenceHint.en: Cross-border operations list naming each job, the State of intended operation, its competent authority and the job's basis

text.en: Add a planning question asking whether any part of the operation is in another Member State.
Include work near a border where the operational volume or buffer crosses it.
Record the State of intended operation and the name and contact of its competent authority.
Record whether the job is authorised, declared or flown under an LUC.

title.en: Prepare the Article 13 application for an authorised operation in another Member State

description.en: Article 13(1) requires an operator whose operation is authorised to send the competent authority of the State of intended operation a copy of the operational authorisation and the locations, with updated mitigations where needed for the risks specific to the local airspace, terrain, population and climate. Prepare the application from the original risk assessment, adapted to the new location.

evidenceHint.en: Article 13 application with a copy of the authorisation, the locations and the updated mitigations, and proof of submission

text.en: Attach a copy of the operational authorisation granted by the State of registration.
List the exact locations of the intended operation in the other Member State.
Reassess the local airspace, terrain, population and climate against the original risk assessment.
Write the updated mitigations needed for those local differences.
Submit the application and keep the proof of submission with the job file.

title.en: Send the declaration or LUC terms of approval to the authority of the State of operation

description.en: For a declared operation abroad, Article 13(3) requires a copy of the declaration submitted to the State of registration and a copy of its confirmation of receipt and completeness. For an LUC holder, Article 13(4) requires a copy of the terms of approval and the locations of the intended operation. Send the right set for the job's basis before the first flight.

evidenceHint.en: Copies sent to the State of operation (declaration and confirmation, or LUC terms of approval and locations) with proof of sending

text.en: For a declared operation, gather the declaration and its confirmation of receipt and completeness.
For an LUC operation, gather the terms of approval and the list of intended locations.
Send them to the competent authority of the State of intended operation before the first flight.
Keep proof of sending with the job file.

title.en: Hold an authorised operation abroad until the State of operation confirms the updated mitigations

description.en: Under Article 13(2) an authorised operation in another Member State may start only once that State's competent authority has confirmed the updated mitigations are satisfactory, and the State of registration then records them in the authorisation. Block release of the job until the confirmation is on file, brief crews on the updated mitigations and check the authorisation is updated.

evidenceHint.en: Confirmation from the State of operation dated before the first flight, crew briefing on updated mitigations, and the updated authorisation

text.en: Keep the job unreleased until the confirmation from the State of operation is on file.
Brief the crew on the updated mitigations before they deploy.
Fly only with the mitigations the State of operation confirmed.
Check the State of registration has recorded the updated mitigations in the authorisation.

title.en: Review each cross-border operation file for completeness after the work ends

description.en: After each operation abroad, and at least once a year, check the job file holds the Article 13 submission its basis needed, the confirmation where required, the destination's national requirements check, such as insurance and zones, and any occurrence reported. Fix the planning process wherever a file is incomplete.

evidenceHint.en: Completed cross-border file review listing each item checked and any gap found, with the process change made

text.en: Check the file holds the Article 13 submission the job's basis required.
Check the confirmation was received before the first flight where one was required.
Check the destination's national requirements, such as insurance and zones, were checked.
Record any gap and change the planning process so it does not recur.

templates.title: Security of the operation and protection against unlawful interference
templates.description: Specific-category operations meet the security requirements of the area they take place in, and the operator protects its aircraft, links, controllers and ground stations against unlawful interference and unauthorised access, as UAS.SPEC.050(1)(a)(ii) and (iii) require.
templates.objective: To ensure every specific-category operation meets its area's security requirements and that aircraft, links and ground equipment are protected against unlawful interference and unauthorised access.
templates.successCriteria:
Every operating site with security requirements is recorded with those requirements, and every flight there shows they were met.
Command and control links use the protection the manufacturer provides, controllers and ground stations require individual sign-in, and only manufacturer firmware is installed.
Aircraft, batteries and controllers are stored securely and every issue and return is logged, with no unexplained item at reconciliation.
Every suspected interference, tampering or unauthorised access is reported, the aircraft is checked before it flies again and the event is reviewed.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of operating sites with security requirements and the procedures for working there.
Obtain the configuration of command and control links, controllers and ground stations, with installed firmware versions.
Obtain the equipment issue and return log and the reconciliations for the period.
Obtain reports of suspected interference, tampering or unauthorised access and the follow-up records.

Analysis:
Sample flights at sites with security requirements and confirm each requirement was met and recorded.
Inspect a sample of controllers and ground stations for individual sign-in, link protection enabled and manufacturer firmware.
Compare the issue and return log with the equipment inventory and look for items unaccounted for.
Read each interference or tampering report and confirm the aircraft was checked before its next flight and the event reviewed.

Output:
