A list of sites or flights where security requirements were not met.
A list of devices with shared accounts, disabled link protection or non-manufacturer firmware.
A list of equipment unaccounted for and of reports not followed up.

title.en: Identify the security requirements that apply to each specific-category operating site

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(a)(ii) requires procedures ensuring that security requirements applicable to the area of operations are complied with. Sites such as critical infrastructure, prisons, airports, ports and public events often carry their own conditions, and Member States may set geographical zones for security reasons. Record the requirements for each site before work is planned there.

evidenceHint.en: Site security register listing each operating site, the security requirements that apply and their source

text.en: List the operating sites where specific-category work is flown or planned.
Ask each site owner for its security conditions, such as access, escorts and notice periods.
Check whether any geographical zone set for security reasons covers the site.
Record each requirement with its source and the date it was confirmed.

title.en: Write procedures for crews working at sites with security requirements

description.en: Turn each site's security requirements into instructions the crew follows: how access is arranged, who escorts them, which notifications are made to site security, what identification the crew carries and what they do if challenged or told to stop. Include the steps to take when a requirement cannot be met on the day, which is to not fly.

evidenceHint.en: Approved site security procedures covering access, escort, notifications, identification and the response when challenged

text.en: Write how site access is arranged and confirmed before the crew travels.
State which notifications to site security are made, by whom and when.
Require the crew to carry identification and the job authorisation on site.
Tell the crew to stop and not fly whenever a site requirement cannot be met.

title.en: Protect command and control links, controllers and ground stations against unauthorised access

description.en: UAS.SPEC.050(1)(a)(iii) requires measures to protect against unlawful interference and unauthorised access. Keep the link protection the manufacturer provides switched on, give each person their own sign-in to controllers, apps and ground stations, install only manufacturer firmware and apps, and control which controller may pair with which aircraft.

evidenceHint.en: Configuration record per controller and ground station showing link protection on, individual accounts, manufacturer firmware versions and pairing list

text.en: Keep the manufacturer's link encryption or protection enabled and forbid disabling it.
Give each person their own account on controllers, apps and ground stations.
Install only firmware and apps published by the manufacturer and record the versions.
Keep a list of which controllers may pair with which aircraft and remove stale pairings.
Remove access the same day a person leaves or changes role.

title.en: Track the storage, issue and return of aircraft, batteries and controllers

description.en: An aircraft or controller taken without authority is unauthorised access in its simplest form. Store specific-category equipment locked, issue it against a log that names the person and the job, check it back in after the job, and reconcile the log with the inventory regularly so a missing item is noticed and reported quickly.

evidenceHint.en: Equipment issue and return log for the period and the reconciliations against the inventory, with any missing item reported

text.en: Keep aircraft, batteries and controllers in a locked store when not in use.
Log every issue with the person, the job and the time, and every return.
Reconcile the log with the inventory at least weekly.
Report any missing item to the security lead on the day it is found.

title.en: Triage suspected interference, tampering or loss of link integrity during operations

description.en: Pilots need to recognise and act on signs of unlawful interference: an unexpected loss of link or position, a controller behaving as if another station had control, or an aircraft that shows signs of tampering. Land or terminate as the procedure requires, report the event, quarantine the aircraft until it is checked, and inform site security or the police where interference may be deliberate.

evidenceHint.en: Reports of suspected interference or tampering with the actions taken, the aircraft check before return to service and any notification made

text.en: Land or terminate the flight as the procedure requires on signs of interference.
Report the event the same day with the time, place and what was observed.
Quarantine the aircraft and controller until they are checked and cleared.
Inform site security or the police where the interference may be deliberate.

title.en: Review security events and equipment access lists each quarter

description.en: Each quarter, read the interference, tampering and missing-equipment reports, check each was followed up, and review who holds accounts on controllers, apps and ground stations against the current staff list. Look for patterns, such as interference at one site, and update the site register and procedures accordingly.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly security review record listing events reviewed, follow-up status, account review results and changes made

text.en: List the quarter's interference, tampering and missing-equipment reports.
Confirm each was followed up and the aircraft cleared before it flew again.
Compare account holders on controllers and ground stations with the current staff list.
Update the site register and procedures wherever a pattern appears.

templates.title: Competent-authority access and oversight readiness
templates.description: Any person the competent authority authorises can be given access, without delay, to the facilities, aircraft, documents, records, data and procedures relevant to declared or authorised activity, including activity contracted or subcontracted to another organisation.
templates.objective: To ensure the operator can give a person authorised by the competent authority prompt access to everything relevant to its declared or authorised activity, including subcontracted work.
templates.successCriteria:
An index lists the facilities, aircraft, documents, records, data and procedures relevant to declared or authorised activity, with where each is kept.
A named contact and a deputy receive inspections, check the inspector's authorisation and record what was seen.
Every contract for subcontracted activity relevant to declared or authorised operations obliges the subcontractor to grant the same access.
Every inspection and request in the period is logged with its findings and their closure, and the yearly mock inspection produced each indexed item.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the access index of facilities, aircraft, documents, records, data and procedures.
Obtain the inspection procedure, the named contact and deputy, and the inspection log for the period.
Obtain the contracts with organisations to which declared or authorised activity is contracted or subcontracted.
Obtain the results of the last mock inspection and any findings raised by the competent authority.

Analysis:
Compare the index with the operator's declared or authorised activity and note anything relevant that is missing.
Read each relevant contract for a clause obliging the subcontractor to grant access to persons authorised by the competent authority.
Trace each logged inspection to its findings and confirm each finding was answered and closed.
Compare the mock inspection with the index and note each item that could not be produced or took too long.

Output:
A list of relevant items missing from the index.
A list of contracts without an access clause.
A list of open authority findings and of items the mock inspection could not produce.

title.en: List the facilities, aircraft, documents and records an authorised inspector may ask to see

description.en: UAS.SPEC.090 entitles any person duly authorised by the competent authority to access any facility, UAS, document, record, data, procedure or other material relevant to declared or authorised activity, whether done in-house or contracted out. Build an index of that material and where each item is kept, so access can be given quickly and nothing relevant is overlooked.

evidenceHint.en: Access index listing each facility, aircraft, document set, record store and procedure relevant to declared or authorised activity, with its location

text.en: List the sites, hangars and stores used for declared or authorised activity.
List the aircraft, controllers and ground stations in that activity.
List the declarations, authorisations, manuals, procedures and record stores, with their locations.
Add the material held by organisations to which the activity is contracted or subcontracted.

title.en: Name the contact who receives and hosts competent-authority inspections

description.en: An inspection that arrives unannounced should not stall while staff work out who decides. Name a contact and a deputy who receive inspections, write how they check the inspector's authorisation, give access to the indexed material, and record what was seen and taken, and tell all staff to direct an inspector to them.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection procedure naming the contact and deputy, the authorisation check and the recording of what was seen

text.en: Name a contact and a deputy for competent-authority inspections.
Write how they check that the person is duly authorised by the competent authority.
Require them to record what was seen, copied or taken during the visit.
Tell all staff to refer an inspector to the contact and not to refuse access.

title.en: Bind subcontractors to grant the competent authority the same access

description.en: UAS.SPEC.090 covers activity contracted or subcontracted to another organisation, so the operator must be able to give access there too. Add a clause to every relevant contract obliging the subcontractor to give persons authorised by the competent authority access to its facilities, equipment, records and procedures for the work done for the operator.

evidenceHint.en: Access clause wording and a list of relevant contracts showing the clause is included in each

text.en: List the organisations that carry out any part of declared or authorised activity.
Draft a clause obliging each to grant access to persons authorised by the competent authority.
Add the clause to each contract at signature or the next renewal.
Record which contracts carry the clause and chase those that do not.

title.en: Log every competent-authority inspection, request and finding through to closure

description.en: Keep a log of every inspection, information request and finding from the competent authority, with the response and the date each finding was closed. For a declared operation remember that refusing access means the declaration is no longer considered complete under UAS.SPEC.085(3), so any difficulty in giving access is escalated to the accountable manager at once.

evidenceHint.en: Inspection log listing each visit or request, the material provided, the findings and their closure dates

text.en: Log each inspection or request with the date, the inspector and what was asked for.
Record each finding with an owner, a response and a due date.
Escalate any difficulty in giving access to the accountable manager the same day.
Close each finding only when the competent authority's response is on file.

title.en: Run a yearly mock inspection against the access index

description.en: Once a year, have someone play the inspector and ask for a sample of items from the access index, including material held by a subcontractor. Time how long each item takes to produce, record anything that could not be found or that the index did not list, and update the index and procedure.

evidenceHint.en: Mock inspection record listing items requested, time to produce each, gaps found and index updates made

text.en: Choose a sample of indexed items, including at least one held by a subcontractor.
Ask the named contact to produce each one and time the response.
Record items that could not be produced or were missing from the index.
Update the index and the inspection procedure with what the exercise found.

templates.title: Standard-scenario declaration, confirmation and two-year validity
templates.description: Every flight under STS-01 or STS-02 rests on a declaration filed with the competent authority of the State of registration, starts only once that authority confirms receipt and completeness, and stays covered while changes are notified and the declaration's two-year life is renewed in time.
templates.objective: To ensure no standard-scenario flight starts without a complete, confirmed declaration in force, and that changes and the two-year expiry never leave one lapsed.
templates.successCriteria:
Each standard scenario the operator flies is covered by an operational declaration on the Appendix 2 form, filed with the competent authority of the State of registration.
No flight under a scenario took place before the authority's confirmation of receipt and completeness for that declaration.
Every change to the information in a declaration is notified to the authority, and the notification date is recorded.
Every declaration is renewed before its two-year duration ends, and none relies on a national standard scenario.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain every operational declaration the operator has filed, with the submission record and the authority's confirmation of receipt and completeness for each.
Obtain the register of changes notified to the authority in the period and the operator's change log.
Obtain flight logs for operations flown under STS-01 or STS-02 in the period.

Analysis:
Check that each declaration names the operator's registration number, every aircraft by manufacturer, model and serial number, the scenario, and the insurance confirmation where Union or national law requires cover.
Compare the date of the first flight under each scenario with the date of its confirmation and list flights that came earlier.
Compare the change log, including new aircraft, address and insurance changes, with the notifications sent to the authority.
Compute each declaration's two-year expiry and compare it with the flights flown under it and any renewal filed.
Confirm no flight relied on a national standard scenario, which ceased to be valid on 1 January 2026.

Output:
A list of declarations with filing, confirmation and expiry dates.
A list of flights flown before confirmation or after expiry.
A list of changes not notified, or notified late.

title.en: Map each declared operation to STS-01 or STS-02 and to the declaration envelope

description.en: Before filing, check that the operation fits the conditions a declaration can cover under UAS.SPEC.020(1): the aircraft's maximum characteristic dimension for the VLOS or BVLOS case, flight below 120 m, and either uncontrolled airspace or controlled airspace with published procedures that keep the chance of meeting manned aircraft low. Then name the one standard scenario it falls under. An operation that fits neither scenario needs an operational authorisation instead.

evidenceHint.en: Scenario mapping per planned operation naming STS-01 or STS-02, the UAS.SPEC.020(1) conditions checked and the reviewer

text.en: Check the aircraft's maximum characteristic dimension against the VLOS or BVLOS case the operation uses.
Confirm the operation stays below 120 m from the closest point of the surface of the earth.
Record whether the airspace is class F or G, or controlled with published procedures for the area.
Name the scenario, STS-01 or STS-02, and the class of aircraft it requires.
Route any operation that fits neither scenario to the operational authorisation process.

title.en: File the operational declaration on the Appendix 2 form with the State of registration

description.en: Complete the Appendix 2 declaration for each scenario and send it to the competent authority of the Member State where the operator is registered. List every aircraft that will fly under it, including any used only for practical-skill training, as GM1 Appendix 2 allows several aircraft on one form. State that the operator complies with Regulation (EU) 2019/947 and the scenario, and confirm insurance cover where Union or national law requires it.

evidenceHint.en: Copy of the signed declaration as filed, with the submission receipt and the date sent

text.en: Enter the operator registration number and the operator's name as registered.
List the manufacturer, model and serial number of each aircraft, training aircraft included.
Check the national requirements matrix and confirm insurance cover where the law requires it.
Sign and date the declaration and send it to the competent authority of the State of registration.
Store the filed copy and the submission receipt with the operator's declaration records.

title.en: Hold standard-scenario flights until the confirmation of receipt and completeness arrives

description.en: Under UAS.SPEC.020(4) the operator is entitled to start only after the competent authority has confirmed that the declaration is received and complete. Block scheduling of flights under the scenario until that confirmation is on file, then release the scenario for planning and give pilots the confirmation reference. Keep the confirmation with the declaration, because it is also what a foreign authority asks for before a declared operation abroad.

evidenceHint.en: Authority confirmation of receipt and completeness, with the date the scenario was released for flight scheduling

text.en: Mark the scenario as not yet flyable in the scheduling tool when the declaration is filed.
Record the date and reference of the authority's confirmation when it arrives.
Release the scenario for planning only after the confirmation is on file.
Give remote pilots the confirmation reference to carry with the declaration.

title.en: Notify the competent authority of each change to a filed declaration without delay

description.en: UAS.SPEC.020(5) requires the operator to notify any change to the information in a declaration without delay. List the events that trigger a notification, such as a new or replaced aircraft, a changed serial number, new contact or address details, a different accountable manager or a change to insurance cover, and make each one start a notification the same week. Keep the record of what was sent and when.

evidenceHint.en: Change log entries paired with the notification sent to the authority and its date

text.en: List the events that change a declaration, including new aircraft, contact details and insurance.
Add a declaration check to the change processes for fleet, contacts and insurance.
Send the notification to the competent authority as soon as a trigger occurs.
Record the date sent and update the stored copy of the declaration to match.

title.en: Track each declaration's two-year expiry and the conditions that make it incomplete

description.en: A declaration lasts two years under UAS.SPEC.085 and stops counting as complete earlier if oversight finds operations departing from it, if conditions change so it no longer complies, or if the authority is refused access. Record each expiry date, set a renewal reminder well ahead of it, and review the three early-loss conditions every year so a lapsed declaration is found by the operator, not by the authority.

evidenceHint.en: Declaration expiry register with renewal dates and the annual review of the UAS.SPEC.085 conditions

text.en: Record the two-year expiry of each declaration from its confirmation date.
Set a renewal reminder three months before each expiry and assign an owner.
Check for oversight findings that operations departed from the declaration.
Check whether a change in conditions means the declaration no longer complies.
Confirm no flight relies on a national standard scenario declaration.

templates.title: Operations manual and emergency response plan for standard scenarios
templates.description: Standard-scenario operations follow an operations manual with the Appendix 5 contents and an emergency response plan, whose contingency and emergency procedures have been shown adequate by flight test or representative simulation, and which every member of staff has been informed of.
templates.objective: To ensure every declared operation runs to a complete operations manual and a tested emergency response plan that staff know and that stay current with the operation.
templates.successCriteria:
An operations manual exists for the declared scenarios, signed by the accountable manager, containing every element Appendix 5 lists.
The emergency response plan sets out how escalation is limited, when authorities are alerted, what counts as an emergency and each person's duties.
Contingency and emergency procedures were shown adequate by a recorded flight test or representative simulation before declared operations began.
Every remote pilot and essential staff member has been informed of the current manual, and changes are made before the operation changes.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current operations manual and emergency response plan for the standard scenarios, with their versions, approval signatures and change history.
Obtain the records of the flight tests or simulations used to validate the contingency and emergency procedures.
Obtain the list of external services the operation relies on and any agreements with their providers.
Obtain the record of staff informed of the manual.

Analysis:
Compare the manual's contents with each element listed in Appendix 5 and note any missing or empty section.
Check that the emergency response plan covers the four points UAS.STS-01.030(4) and UAS.STS-02.030(4) require and names contacts that are current.
Check that the validation records cover the contingency and emergency procedures actually written, and that defects found were corrected.
Check that each external service has a stated level of performance and a documented split of roles with its provider.
Compare the staff list with the record of who was informed of the current version.

Output:
A table of Appendix 5 elements present, partial or missing.
A list of procedures not validated, and of staff not informed of the current manual.
Any external service without a stated performance or role split.

title.en: Draft the standard-scenario operations manual against the Appendix 5 contents

description.en: Appendix 5 lists what an operations manual for a standard scenario must contain at least: a statement of compliance, the accountable manager's approval signature, a description of the organisation, the concept of operation with its area, airspace, environment, operational volume and buffers, the technical means, the personnel and their training, the maintenance instructions and the operational procedures. Lay out the manual against that list so no element is missed. One manual may cover both scenarios.

evidenceHint.en: Operations manual draft with an Appendix 5 cross-reference table showing where each element is addressed

text.en: Build a cross-reference table listing every element Appendix 5 requires.
Describe the organisation, the activities and the risks identified for each scenario.
Describe the area, airspace, weather and electromagnetic environment, volume and buffers.
Describe the aircraft and external systems, and the team's roles, training and recent experience.
Add the manufacturer's maintenance instructions and the statement of compliance.

title.en: Write the normal, contingency and emergency procedures for declared operations

description.en: The procedures in the manual must be based on the manufacturer's instructions and, per the AMC, meet the medium level of robustness in AMC2 UAS.SPEC.030(3)(e). Cover pre-flight preparation and checklists, including the assessment of the volume and buffers and securing the controlled ground area, launch and recovery, keeping the aircraft in the flight geography, post-flight inspection, contingency procedures for abnormal situations and emergency procedures that include triggering flight termination.

evidenceHint.en: Procedures section of the operations manual covering normal, contingency and emergency phases, cross-referenced to the manufacturer's instructions

text.en: Write pre-flight checklists covering the volume, buffers, environment and controlled ground area.
Assign each task to a named role and add an internal checklist that confirms it was done.
Write launch, recovery, in-flight and post-flight inspection procedures.
Write contingency procedures for when the aircraft may leave the flight geography.
Write emergency procedures, including when and how to trigger flight termination.

title.en: Build the emergency response plan for standard-scenario operations

description.en: Both scenarios require an emergency response plan that contains at least the plan to limit the escalating effects of an emergency, the conditions for alerting the relevant authorities and organisations, the criteria that identify an emergency, and a clear split of duties between the remote pilots and other essential staff. The AMC asks for the medium level of robustness in AMC3 UAS.SPEC.030(3)(e). Put contact details for each site's emergency services and authorities in the plan.

evidenceHint.en: Emergency response plan with the four required elements, a duty table per role and the site contact list, with its version and approval

text.en: Define the criteria that identify an emergency, such as a fly-away or an injury on the ground.
Write the actions that limit escalation once an emergency is identified.
State when and how the relevant authorities and organisations are alerted.
Assign the duties of the remote pilot and each other essential role in an emergency.
List the emergency services and authority contacts for each operating site.

title.en: Validate the contingency and emergency procedures by flight test or representative simulation

description.en: UAS.STS-01.030(3) and UAS.STS-02.030(3) require the operator to show the contingency and emergency procedures are adequate, by dedicated flight tests or by simulation whose representativeness suits the purpose. The AMC allows the flight test to be flown in subcategory A3 of the open category, as long as that flight complies with the open-category rules. Record each test, what it showed and any change it forced.

evidenceHint.en: Validation record per procedure naming the method, date, conditions, result and the procedure change it led to

text.en: List each contingency and emergency procedure that needs validating.
Choose a flight test or a simulation for each, and justify why a simulation is representative.
Fly any validation test in subcategory A3 under the open-category rules.
Record the result of each test and correct any procedure that did not work.
File the validation records with the operations manual version they validated.

title.en: Review external services and the operations manual's currency each year

description.en: Any service provided by someone else that the flight's safety depends on, such as a positioning or communication service, needs an adequate level of performance and a defined split of roles between the operator and the provider. Review those each year, amend the manual whenever the operation changes, and keep a record that remote pilots and essential staff have been informed of the current version, as UAS.SPEC.050(1)(d)(v) and (e)(ii) require.

evidenceHint.en: Annual review record covering external services, manual amendments made and the staff informed of the current version

text.en: List each external service the operation's safety depends on and its provider.
Confirm the performance each service must deliver and that it was delivered.
Confirm the roles and responsibilities agreed with each provider are written down.
Amend the manual for any change in aircraft, sites, staff or procedures.
Record that each remote pilot and essential staff member was informed of the new version.

templates.title: Standard-scenario theoretical certificate and practical-skill accreditation
templates.description: Every remote pilot flying a standard scenario holds the certificate of remote pilot theoretical knowledge for the standard scenarios and, for each scenario flown, an accreditation of completion of its practical skill training from an entity or operator that has declared compliance with Appendix 3.
templates.objective: To ensure only pilots holding a valid standard-scenario theoretical certificate and the practical-skill accreditation for that scenario are rostered for declared operations.
templates.successCriteria:
Every pilot rostered under a standard scenario holds a valid certificate of remote pilot theoretical knowledge for operations in the standard scenarios.
Each such pilot holds an accreditation of completion of the practical skill training for every scenario they fly, from an entity that has declared compliance with Appendix 3.
No pilot flies a scenario they hold no accreditation for.
Each certificate is revalidated within its five-year validity, or by the examination route once expired.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the roster of remote pilots for standard-scenario operations, with their theoretical certificates and practical-skill accreditations.
Obtain the records of who issued each accreditation and the declaration that entity or operator made under Appendix 3.
Obtain flight logs for declared operations in the period, naming the pilot and scenario of each flight.

Analysis:
Check each certificate's issuer, identification number and dates, and confirm the holder passed the A1/A3 online examination before the additional examination.
Check that each accreditation names the scenario and comes from a recognised entity or a declared operator, and that progress booklets exist where the operator trained the pilot itself.
Match every flight in the sample to the pilot's certificate and the accreditation for that scenario on the flight date.
Compute each certificate's five-year expiry and check revalidations were done by examination or refresher within validity.

Output:
A table of pilots with certificate expiry and the scenarios they are accredited for.
A list of flights flown without the matching accreditation or with an expired certificate.
A list of certificates due within six months.

title.en: Define the standard-scenario credentials a remote pilot must hold before rostering

description.en: Write down what a pilot needs to fly declared operations. One certificate of remote pilot theoretical knowledge covers both scenarios; the practical skill accreditation is per scenario, so a pilot accredited for STS-01 is not thereby accredited for STS-02. Record for each credential its identification number in the NNN-RP form, the issuing authority or entity and its dates, so the roster can test them.

evidenceHint.en: Credential requirement statement for STS-01 and STS-02 and the roster fields that record each credential

text.en: State that the theoretical certificate for the standard scenarios is required for any declared flight.
State that a separate practical-skill accreditation is needed for each scenario flown.
Add roster fields for the certificate number, issuer, issue date and expiry.
Add a roster field for each scenario accreditation and who issued it.

title.en: Enrol remote pilots in the standard-scenario theoretical knowledge examination

description.en: A pilot first completes the A1/A3 online training and examination, then passes an additional examination set by the competent authority or its designated entity under Attachment A. It has at least 40 multiple-choice questions on aviation regulations, human performance, operational procedures, ground-risk and air-risk mitigations, UAS general knowledge, meteorology and flight performance, or at least 30 on the first five subjects for a pilot holding the A2 certificate. The pass mark is 75%.

evidenceHint.en: Examination booking and result for each pilot, and a copy of the certificate of remote pilot theoretical knowledge issued

text.en: Confirm the pilot holds proof of the A1/A3 online training and examination.
Check whether the pilot holds the A2 certificate, which shortens the examination.
Book the additional examination with the competent authority or its designated entity.
Record the result and store a copy of the certificate in the pilot's training file.

title.en: Obtain an STS practical-skill accreditation for each scenario a pilot will fly

description.en: The accreditation of completion of the practical skill training must come from an entity recognised by the competent authority that has declared compliance with Appendix 3, or from an operator that has declared the scenario and declared Appendix 3 compliance using the Appendix 4 form. An operator that trains in another Member State sends a copy of its Appendix 4 form to that State's authority. Keep the progress booklet the instructor compiles and the student signs.

evidenceHint.en: Accreditation per pilot and scenario, the issuer's Appendix 3 declaration reference and the signed progress booklet

text.en: Choose a recognised training entity or confirm the operator's own Appendix 4 declaration is filed.
Send a copy of the Appendix 4 form to the authority where training happens, if in another State.
Keep the progress booklet signed by the student pilot after each practical session.
Record the accreditation, the scenario it covers and its issuer in the roster.

title.en: Hold back any pilot from a scenario they hold no accreditation for

description.en: Make the roster refuse an assignment that the pilot's credentials do not support. A pilot with the theoretical certificate but only an STS-01 accreditation is not available for STS-02 work, and a pilot whose certificate has expired is not available for either. Check the pilot carries proof of competency on the day, as UAS.SPEC.060(1)(b) requires.

evidenceHint.en: Rostering rule configured or checklist used, with records of assignments refused for missing credentials

text.en: Check the pilot's certificate is in date before assigning a declared flight.
Check the pilot holds the accreditation for the scenario of that flight.
Refuse the assignment and name a qualified pilot when either check fails.
Confirm on the day that the pilot carries proof of competency.

title.en: Schedule revalidation of standard-scenario theoretical certificates within five years

description.en: The theoretical certificate is valid for five years. Within that period it is revalidated either by demonstrating the competencies again or by a refresher training on the examination subjects from the competent authority or its designated entity. Once it has expired, only the full examination route revalidates it. Review expiry dates every quarter so pilots revalidate while the cheaper route is still open.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly expiry review listing certificates due, the revalidation route chosen and the new certificate dates

text.en: List every certificate expiring in the next twelve months.
Book the refresher training or examination for each pilot due within six months.
Withdraw from declared operations any pilot whose certificate has expired.
Record the new certificate and its expiry in the roster when revalidation is complete.

templates.title: STS-01 operational volume, ground risk buffer and controlled ground area
templates.description: For each STS-01 site the operator defines the operational volume and the ground risk buffer, using the regulation's table for the buffer, and has a controlled ground area covering both in place, with everyone inside it briefed and consenting, before the first take-off in a populated environment.
templates.objective: To ensure every STS-01 operation flies inside a defined volume over a controlled ground area sized by the regulation's buffer table and secured before flight in a populated area.
templates.successCriteria:
Each STS-01 site has a recorded flight geography, a contingency area at least 10 m beyond it and an operational volume no more than 30 m above the 120 m limit.
Each ground risk buffer is at least the table value for the planned height and the aircraft's mass, or the tether length plus 5 m for a tethered aircraft.
The controlled ground area covers the volume and buffer and was in place and effective before take-off.
Everyone inside the controlled ground area was informed of the risks, briefed and recorded as explicitly agreeing to take part.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the site files for STS-01 operations in the period, with their maps of flight geography, contingency area, ground risk buffer and controlled ground area.
Obtain the buffer calculations, the pre-flight records showing the controlled ground area was set up, and any coordination with local authorities.
Obtain the briefing and agreement records for people inside the controlled ground area.

Analysis:
Check that each contingency area extends at least 10 m beyond the flight geography and that the operational volume does not rise more than 30 m above the 120 m limit.
Recompute each ground risk buffer from the planned height and the aircraft's mass using the table in UAS.STS-01.020, and for tethered aircraft from the tether length plus 5 m.
Compare the controlled ground area on each map with the projection of the volume and buffer, and check it was in place before the first take-off.
Match the people recorded on site with the agreement records.

Output:
A list of sites with buffers below the table value or contingency areas narrower than 10 m.
A list of operations started before the controlled ground area was in place.
A list of people present without a recorded briefing and agreement.

title.en: Define the STS-01 flight geography, contingency area and operational volume for each site

description.en: Draw the volume each STS-01 operation will use: the flight geography where the aircraft is meant to fly, a contingency area whose outer limit is at least 10 m beyond it, and a height no greater than 120 m above the closest point of the surface, or 15 m above an obstacle taller than 105 m within 50 m of it when the entity responsible for the obstacle asks for that. The operational volume may not rise more than 30 m above that limit, and no dangerous goods are carried.

evidenceHint.en: Site map with flight geography, contingency area and maximum height drawn, and the obstacle permission where one is used

text.en: Draw the flight geography the operation needs on the site map.
Add a contingency area whose outer limit lies at least 10 m beyond the flight geography.
Set the maximum height at 120 m, or 15 m above a qualifying obstacle at its owner's request.
Cap the operational volume at no more than 30 m above that maximum height.
Confirm the operation carries no dangerous goods.

title.en: Determine the STS-01 ground risk buffer from the height and mass table

description.en: The ground risk buffer for an untethered STS-01 aircraft comes from the table in UAS.STS-01.020: at a maximum height of 30 m it is 10 m up to 10 kg MTOM and 20 m above, at 60 m it is 15 m and 30 m, at 90 m 20 m and 45 m, and at 120 m 25 m and 60 m. A tethered aircraft needs a radius of the tether length plus 5 m around the fixing point. The AMC treats these as minimums, so add margin for wind and the aircraft's behaviour.

evidenceHint.en: Buffer calculation per site showing planned height, MTOM, table value, any added margin and the final buffer drawn

text.en: Look up the table value for the planned maximum height and the aircraft's MTOM.
Use the tether length plus 5 m as the radius instead for a tethered aircraft.
Add margin for wind, the aircraft's flight characteristics and the pilot's reaction time.
Draw the final buffer beyond the contingency area on the site map.
Record the calculation with the site file and the name of who checked it.

title.en: Establish the STS-01 controlled ground area before the first take-off

description.en: The controlled ground area covers the ground beneath the operational volume and the ground risk buffer, and in a populated environment it has to be made to work: barriers, signs, marshals or a closed site that keep uninvolved people out for the duration. UAS.STS-01.030(8) requires it to be in place, effective and compliant with the buffer distance before the operation starts, with coordination with the appropriate authorities when required, and geo-awareness updated where the zone calls for it.

evidenceHint.en: Pre-flight record that the controlled ground area was set up and checked, with any authority coordination and the geo-awareness update

text.en: Mark the controlled ground area on the map so it covers the volume and the buffer.
Choose the means of keeping people out, such as barriers, marshals or a site closure.
Coordinate with the local authority or landowner where closing the area requires it.
Walk the perimeter before take-off and confirm no uninvolved person is inside.
Load updated zone data into geo-awareness when the zone for the site requires it.

title.en: Brief everyone inside the STS-01 controlled ground area and record their explicit agreement

description.en: Under UAS.STS-01.030(9), before the operation starts every person present in the controlled ground area must have been informed of its risks, briefed or trained as appropriate on the safety precautions the operator has set, and have explicitly agreed to take part. Anyone who does not agree is not a participant and must be outside the area before the aircraft flies. Brief late arrivals before they enter.

evidenceHint.en: Briefing and agreement sheet for each operation, listing each person in the controlled ground area, the briefing given and their agreement

text.en: List every person who will be inside the controlled ground area during the operation.
Explain the risks and the safety precautions, such as safe positions and the fly-away drill.
Record each person's explicit agreement to take part, with their name and the time.
Ask anyone who does not agree to leave the area before take-off.
Brief and record anyone who arrives after the operation has started before they enter.

title.en: Audit STS-01 sites against their recorded volume, buffer and controlled ground area

description.en: Each month sample STS-01 operations and compare what was planned with what happened: was the buffer at least the table value for the height actually flown, did the track stay in the flight geography, was the controlled ground area in place before take-off, and does the agreement sheet list everyone the logs show inside it? Raise a finding for each gap and check it is closed.

evidenceHint.en: Monthly audit worksheet of sampled STS-01 operations, the checks made and the findings raised with owners

text.en: Select a sample of STS-01 operations from the month across different sites.
Compare the maximum height flown with the height the buffer was sized for.
Overlay the flight track on the site map and check it stayed in the flight geography.
Check the controlled ground area record and the agreement sheet for each operation.
Raise a finding with an owner and due date for each gap found.

templates.title: STS-01 class C5 aircraft and flight termination
templates.description: Only class C5 aircraft, or class C3 aircraft fitted with the C5 accessories kit, fly STS-01, each accompanied by its declaration of conformity and labelled, with direct remote identification active and its flight termination means checked before every flight.
templates.objective: To ensure every STS-01 flight uses an aircraft whose C5 basis is documented and intact, with working flight termination and active, up-to-date remote identification.
templates.successCriteria:
Every aircraft used for STS-01 is a class C5 aircraft or a class C3 aircraft fitted with the C5 accessories kit.
Each is accompanied by the declarations of conformity naming class C5, or class C3 and the accessories kit, and carries the C5 label on the aircraft or the kit.
Before every STS-01 flight the pilot recorded that the flight termination means work and remote identification is active and up to date.
An aircraft whose kit or label was removed or changed is withdrawn from STS-01 until its C5 basis is restored.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the fleet register entries for aircraft used under STS-01, with their declarations of conformity and photographs of the class labels.
Obtain the pre-flight checklists for STS-01 flights in the period.
Obtain the maintenance and repair records for those aircraft.

Analysis:
Check each aircraft's declaration of conformity names class C5, or class C3 with the C5 accessories kit, and that the serial numbers match the register.
Check a label photograph exists for each aircraft or kit and is dated after the latest repair.
Sample STS-01 flights and confirm the pre-flight checklist records both the flight termination check and the remote identification check.
Compare maintenance records with flight logs to find flights after a kit or label change that preceded a recorded re-check.
Match the aircraft serial numbers in the flight logs with those listed in the declaration filed for STS-01.

Output:
A list of aircraft used under STS-01 without a matching declaration of conformity or label.
A list of flights missing the termination or remote identification check.
Any flight made after the C5 basis was disturbed and not restored.

title.en: Confirm each aircraft assigned to STS-01 has a documented class C5 basis

description.en: STS-01 can be flown only with a class C5 aircraft, or a class C3 aircraft fitted with the C5 accessories kit, complying with Part 16 of the Annex to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/945. UAS.STS-01.030(10) requires the declarations of conformity naming class C5, or class C3 and the kit, to accompany the aircraft and the C5 label to be on the aircraft or the kit. An aircraft without that basis needs an operational authorisation, such as under PDRA-S01, not a declaration.

evidenceHint.en: Fleet register entries flagged as STS-01 eligible, each with the declaration of conformity and a label photograph

text.en: Check the aircraft's declaration of conformity names class C5, or class C3 and the C5 kit.
Photograph the C5 label on the aircraft or the accessories kit and attach it to the register.
Match the serial number on the aircraft with the declaration and the register entry.
Flag the aircraft as eligible for STS-01 only when all three checks pass.
Route any aircraft that fails to the operational authorisation process instead.

title.en: Configure direct remote identification on every STS-01 aircraft

description.en: UAS.STS-01.020(1)(f) requires the aircraft to be operated with active and updated direct remote identification. Load the operator registration number with its secret digits into each aircraft, confirm the system accepts the string without an error message, and set up a re-check after every firmware update, repair or swap of the remote identification module.

evidenceHint.en: Remote identification configuration record per aircraft with the date loaded, the check result and the re-check trigger list

text.en: Load the operator registration number and secret digits into the remote identification system.
Confirm the aircraft shows no error message for the loaded string.
Confirm with a receiving mobile device that the broadcast carries the operator number.
List firmware updates, repairs and module swaps as triggers for a re-check.

title.en: Verify the STS-01 flight termination means and remote identification before each flight

description.en: UAS.STS-01.040(1) requires the remote pilot, before every operation, to verify that the means to terminate the flight are operational and that direct remote identification is active and up to date. Make both items mandatory on the STS-01 pre-flight checklist so a flight cannot be marked ready without them, and record the result in the flight log.

evidenceHint.en: Pre-flight checklist entries for each STS-01 flight showing the termination and remote identification checks and their result

text.en: Run the manufacturer's check of the flight termination means before the first flight of the day.
Confirm remote identification is active and shows the correct operator number.
Record both results on the pre-flight checklist before take-off.
Ground the aircraft and report it if either check fails.

title.en: Inspect the C5 accessories kit and label after any maintenance or repair

description.en: A class C3 aircraft keeps its STS-01 eligibility only while the C5 accessories kit is fitted, and any aircraft only while its C5 label and conformity are intact. After maintenance, repair or a part replacement, inspect the kit and label and confirm the work followed the manufacturer's instructions. If the kit was removed or changed, or the label is missing, withdraw the aircraft from STS-01 until it is restored.

evidenceHint.en: Post-maintenance inspection record confirming kit, label and conformity, or the withdrawal from STS-01 and its reason

text.en: Inspect the accessories kit and the C5 label after each maintenance or repair job.
Confirm the work and any parts used followed the manufacturer's instructions.
Withdraw the aircraft from STS-01 in the register if the kit or label is not intact.
Record the inspection date and result in the aircraft's register entry.

title.en: Review each quarter that every STS-01 flight used an eligible C5 aircraft

description.en: Each quarter compare the aircraft serial numbers in STS-01 flight logs with the register's STS-01 eligibility flags and with the aircraft listed in the filed declaration. A flight with an aircraft not flagged, not declared or withdrawn after maintenance is a finding, and a newly added aircraft also means the declaration must be updated with the authority.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly reconciliation of STS-01 flight logs against the fleet register and the filed declaration, with findings raised

text.en: Export the aircraft serial numbers from the quarter's STS-01 flight logs.
Match each serial number with an STS-01 eligible entry in the fleet register.
Match each serial number with the aircraft listed in the filed declaration.
Raise a finding for every flight with an aircraft that fails either match.
Notify the authority of any aircraft that should be added to the declaration.

templates.title: STS-01 remote pilot flight duties
templates.description: During STS-01 flights the remote pilot keeps the aircraft in visual line of sight below 5 m/s ground speed, scans the airspace for manned aircraft, controls one aircraft at a time from a fixed position, and applies the contingency and emergency procedures when the flight geography or volume is threatened.
templates.objective: To ensure STS-01 remote pilots fly within visual line of sight and the speed limit and act on the contingency and emergency procedures when the aircraft may leave its limits.
templates.successCriteria:
STS-01 flight logs show the aircraft in visual line of sight throughout and, untethered, below 5 m/s ground speed.
No STS-01 flight was flown from a moving vehicle, with more than one aircraft per pilot, or with control handed to another command unit.
Where an unmanned aircraft observer assisted, the log records the communication means agreed between pilot and observer.
Each remote pilot has exercised the contingency procedure and the flight-termination emergency procedure within the past year.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the STS-01 flight logs, telemetry or track exports and pre-flight checklists for the period.
Obtain the operator's STS-01 pilot checklist and the records of contingency and emergency drills.
Obtain any occurrence reports from STS-01 operations.

Analysis:
Sample STS-01 flights and read the telemetry for ground speed above 5 m/s on untethered aircraft and for distance or obstructions that put the aircraft out of visual line of sight.
Check the logs for flights from a moving vehicle, two aircraft under one pilot or a hand-over of control.
For flights with an observer, check that the communication means was recorded and tested before flight.
Compare the drill records with the pilot roster to find pilots without a contingency or termination drill in the past year.
Read occurrence reports for cases where the aircraft approached the flight geography limit, and check the contingency procedure was applied.

Output:
A list of sampled flights exceeding 5 m/s or leaving visual line of sight.
A list of pilots overdue for a drill.
Any occurrence where the contingency or emergency procedure was not followed.

title.en: Write the STS-01 in-flight rules into the remote pilot checklist

description.en: UAS.STS-01.040(2) sets what the pilot does during flight: keep the aircraft in visual line of sight with a thorough scan of the surrounding airspace, discontinue when the flight poses a risk, keep control except after a lost command and control link, fly one aircraft at a time, never from a moving vehicle, and never hand control to another command unit. UAS.STS-01.020(1)(d) adds a ground speed below 5 m/s for untethered aircraft. Put each rule on the checklist.

evidenceHint.en: STS-01 pilot checklist listing each UAS.STS-01.040(2) rule and the 5 m/s limit, with its version

text.en: List the visual line of sight and airspace scan rule with the duty to discontinue on risk.
List one aircraft per pilot, no moving vehicle and no hand-over to another command unit.
List the ground speed limit below 5 m/s for untethered aircraft.
List when the contingency and emergency procedures must be applied.
Issue the checklist to every STS-01 pilot and record its version.

title.en: Select the C5 low-speed mode on every untethered STS-01 flight

description.en: An untethered class C5 aircraft carries a low-speed mode the remote pilot selects, which limits ground speed to no more than 5 m/s (Part 16 of the Annex to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/945), while STS-01 requires a ground speed below 5 m/s. Make selecting the mode a pre-take-off checklist item, confirm it still engages after power cycles and firmware updates, and keep a margin under the limit that the telemetry review can see.

evidenceHint.en: Checklist item for the low-speed mode and a per-aircraft record that it engages after updates, with telemetry showing ground speed under 5 m/s

text.en: Add selecting the low-speed mode to the STS-01 pre-take-off checklist for untethered aircraft.
Confirm on each C5 aircraft that the mode caps ground speed at no more than 5 m/s.
Re-check that the mode engages after every firmware update and record the result.
Brief pilots to fly with a margin below 5 m/s, since STS-01 requires a speed under it.

title.en: Agree the communication between the STS-01 remote pilot and any unmanned aircraft observer

description.en: An unmanned aircraft observer may help the pilot keep the airspace scan under UAS.STS-01.040(2)(b), but only with clear and effective communication between them. Choose the means, such as radio or direct voice, agree short phrases for traffic, hazards and a call to stop, and test the link at the operating position before each flight.

evidenceHint.en: Observer communication procedure with agreed phrases, and the pre-flight communication check recorded for each flight using an observer

text.en: Choose the communication means between pilot and observer for each site.
Agree short calls for traffic, hazards, loss of sight and stop.
Brief the observer on what to watch for and when to call.
Test the communication at the operating positions before take-off and record it.

title.en: Exercise the STS-01 contingency and flight-termination procedures with each remote pilot

description.en: UAS.STS-01.040(2)(g) and (h) require the pilot to apply the contingency procedures when the aircraft may exceed the flight geography and the emergency procedures, including triggering flight termination, when it may exceed the operational volume. Run a drill with each pilot at least once a year so the response is practised, and record how quickly and correctly it was carried out.

evidenceHint.en: Drill record per pilot naming the scenario, the action taken, the time to act and any retraining given

text.en: Set up a training flight in a safe area where a boundary breach can be simulated.
Have the pilot respond to an aircraft drifting towards the flight geography limit.
Have the pilot respond to an aircraft about to leave the operational volume.
Time each response and note whether the correct procedure was followed.
Retrain any pilot whose response was late or wrong and record it.

title.en: Sample STS-01 flight logs each month for line of sight, speed and procedure compliance

description.en: Each month take a sample of STS-01 flights, read the telemetry for ground speed and distance from the pilot, and check the logs for observers, communication checks and any contingency or emergency event. A flight above 5 m/s, out of visual line of sight or with an unapplied procedure is a finding to follow up with the pilot.

evidenceHint.en: Monthly STS-01 log sample with speed and distance readings, events reviewed and findings raised

text.en: Select a sample of STS-01 flights across pilots and sites from the month.
Read the maximum ground speed and the greatest distance from the pilot for each.
Check each flight with an observer recorded a communication check.
Check each contingency or emergency event against the procedure that should apply.
Raise findings and discuss each one with the pilot concerned.

templates.title: STS-02 operational volume, ground risk buffer and controlled ground area
templates.description: Each STS-02 site lies entirely in a sparsely populated environment, with a flight geography, a contingency area and a ground risk buffer at least as wide as the distance the aircraft is likely to travel after flight termination, and a controlled ground area protected against intrusion before flight.
templates.objective: To ensure every STS-02 operation flies over a controlled ground area in a sparsely populated environment, with a buffer sized from the aircraft's termination behaviour and intrusion risk reduced.
templates.successCriteria:
Each STS-02 site file shows the controlled ground area lies entirely in a sparsely populated environment.
Each site has a flight geography, a contingency area at least 10 m beyond it and an operational volume no more than 30 m above the 120 m limit.
Each ground risk buffer is at least the distance the manufacturer's instructions give for travel after flight termination in the expected conditions.
Intrusion measures were in place and everyone inside the controlled ground area was briefed and agreed before take-off.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the STS-02 site files for the period with their maps, population evidence, buffer calculations and intrusion measures.
Obtain the manufacturer's instructions stating the aircraft's behaviour after flight termination.
Obtain the pre-flight records, authority coordination records and the briefing and agreement sheets.

Analysis:
Check each site's population evidence supports a sparsely populated environment across the whole controlled ground area, not only the flight path.
Check the contingency area and operational volume dimensions against UAS.STS-02.010 and UAS.STS-02.020(2).
Recompute each buffer from the manufacturer's termination distance and the wind and height planned, and compare it with the buffer drawn.
Check that intrusion measures and any required coordination were recorded before the first take-off.
Match the people recorded on site with the agreement sheets.

Output:
A list of sites whose population evidence does not cover the whole controlled ground area.
A list of buffers below the termination distance.
A list of operations started without intrusion measures or agreements recorded.

title.en: Confirm each STS-02 controlled ground area lies entirely in a sparsely populated environment

description.en: UAS.STS-02.020(2) allows STS-02 only over a controlled ground area entirely located in a sparsely populated environment. Check the whole area, buffer included, against current population information such as maps, aerial imagery and a site visit, and note seasonal or event-related crowds. A site where any part is populated cannot be flown under STS-02.

evidenceHint.en: Site population assessment with the sources used, the date checked and the decision for STS-02

text.en: Draw the full controlled ground area, buffer included, on a current map.
Check the area against population maps, aerial imagery and local knowledge.
Visit the site and note any dwellings, roads, paths or gathering places inside it.
Note seasonal uses or events that could bring people into the area.
Reject the site for STS-02 if any part of the area is not sparsely populated.

title.en: Define the STS-02 flight geography, contingency area and operational volume

description.en: Draw the volume for each STS-02 flight: the flight geography the pre-programmed trajectory follows, a contingency area whose outer limit lies at least 10 m beyond it, and a maximum height of 120 m above the closest point of the surface, or 15 m above an obstacle taller than 105 m within 50 m when its owner requests it. The operational volume may not rise more than 30 m above that limit, and no dangerous goods are carried.

evidenceHint.en: Site map with the STS-02 flight geography, contingency area and maximum height, and any obstacle permission

text.en: Draw the flight geography around the planned pre-programmed trajectory.
Add a contingency area at least 10 m beyond the flight geography.
Set the maximum height at 120 m, or 15 m above a qualifying obstacle at its owner's request.
Cap the operational volume at no more than 30 m above that maximum height.
Confirm the operation carries no dangerous goods.

title.en: Derive the STS-02 ground risk buffer from the manufacturer's flight-termination distance

description.en: Unlike STS-01, STS-02 sets no table. UAS.STS-02.020(2)(c) requires a ground risk buffer at least equal to the distance the aircraft is most likely to travel after its flight termination means are activated, as the manufacturer's instructions specify, considering the operational conditions within the manufacturer's limits. Take that distance for the planned height, speed and wind and draw the buffer beyond the contingency area.

evidenceHint.en: Buffer calculation per site citing the manufacturer's termination distance, the conditions assumed and the final buffer drawn

text.en: Find the post-termination travel distance in the manufacturer's instructions.
Select the value for the planned height, speed and the strongest wind allowed.
Draw the buffer at least that wide beyond the contingency area.
Record the calculation and the conditions assumed in the site file.

title.en: Reduce the risk of intrusion into the STS-02 controlled ground area before each operation

description.en: UAS.STS-02.030(8) requires the operator, before starting, to take all appropriate measures to reduce the risk of uninvolved people entering the controlled ground area, and to coordinate with the appropriate authorities when required. In open country that may mean signs at access points, notices to landowners, path closures or lookouts. Update geo-awareness where the zone for the site requires it.

evidenceHint.en: Intrusion-risk measures recorded per operation, with any authority or landowner coordination and the geo-awareness update

text.en: Identify the access points to the controlled ground area, such as tracks and footpaths.
Place signs or lookouts at the access points for the duration of the operation.
Notify landowners and coordinate with the authority where the area requires it.
Load updated zone data into geo-awareness when the zone for the site requires it.
Record the measures taken before the first take-off.

title.en: Brief everyone inside the STS-02 controlled ground area and obtain their agreement

description.en: Before an STS-02 operation starts, UAS.STS-02.030(9) requires every person present in the controlled ground area to have been informed of the risks, briefed and, where applicable, trained on the operator's safety precautions, and to have explicitly agreed to take part. In a large rural area this includes farm workers and others who are there for their own reasons. Anyone who does not agree must be outside the area before flight.

evidenceHint.en: Briefing and agreement record for the STS-02 operation listing each person inside the area and their agreement

text.en: Find out who will be working or present inside the controlled ground area.
Explain the risks and the safety precautions to each of them.
Record each person's explicit agreement with their name and the time.
Make sure anyone who does not agree is outside the area before take-off.

title.en: Re-check STS-02 sites when land use or population around them changes

description.en: A site that was sparsely populated when assessed can change, through new building, a new footpath or a seasonal event. Each month review the STS-02 sites in use, refresh the population assessment of any site where something has changed, and stop STS-02 operations there until the site is reassessed.

evidenceHint.en: Monthly STS-02 site review listing sites checked, changes found and the decision for each

text.en: List every STS-02 site used or planned in the coming month.
Check for new buildings, routes or events reported near each site.
Refresh the population assessment for any site where something changed.
Suspend STS-02 at a site until its reassessment is complete.

templates.title: STS-02 class C6 aircraft, flight-geography limitation and flight termination
templates.description: Only class C6 aircraft fly STS-02, each with its declaration of conformity and label, a programmable flight volume that keeps it within the flight geography, a pre-programmed trajectory beyond visual line of sight, and flight termination checked before every flight.
templates.objective: To ensure every STS-02 flight uses a documented class C6 aircraft held to its flight geography by its programmed volume, with termination and remote identification checked before flight.
templates.successCriteria:
Every aircraft used for STS-02 is a class C6 aircraft accompanied by its declaration of conformity naming class C6 and carrying the C6 label.
Before each STS-02 flight the pilot set the programmable flight volume to the flight geography and recorded the termination and remote identification checks.
The aircraft followed a pre-programmed trajectory whenever it was out of the pilot's visual line of sight, and stayed in sight at launch and recovery.
Without airspace observers no aircraft flew more than 1 km from the remote pilot.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the fleet register entries, declarations of conformity and label photographs for aircraft used under STS-02.
Obtain pre-flight checklists, flight plans with programmed volumes, and telemetry or track exports for STS-02 flights in the period.
Obtain records of any flight termination or flight geography breach.

Analysis:
Check each aircraft's declaration of conformity names class C6 and its serial number matches the register and the filed declaration.
Sample flights and compare the programmed volume with the flight geography on the site map.
Check each sampled pre-flight checklist records the termination, programmable volume and remote identification checks.
Read each sampled track for segments flown out of visual line of sight without a pre-programmed trajectory, and for distance from the pilot above 1 km on flights without observers.
Review each termination or breach event for the contingency or emergency procedure applied.

Output:
A list of aircraft used under STS-02 without a C6 basis on file.
A list of sampled flights with missing checks, a mismatched volume or excess distance.
Any breach of the flight geography and the action taken.

title.en: Confirm each aircraft assigned to STS-02 has a documented class C6 basis

description.en: STS-02 requires an aircraft marked as class C6 under Part 17 of the Annex to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/945. UAS.STS-02.030(11) requires its declaration of conformity naming class C6 to accompany it and the C6 label to be fixed on the aircraft. There is no accessories-kit route to C6 as there is for C5, so an aircraft without the C6 basis needs an operational authorisation, such as under PDRA-S02.

evidenceHint.en: Fleet register entries flagged as STS-02 eligible, each with the C6 declaration of conformity and a label photograph

text.en: Check the aircraft's declaration of conformity names class C6.
Photograph the C6 label on the aircraft and attach it to the register entry.
Match the aircraft's serial number with the declaration and the register.
Flag the aircraft as eligible for STS-02 only when all three checks pass.
Route any aircraft without a C6 basis to the operational authorisation process.

title.en: Set the programmable flight volume so the STS-02 aircraft stays within the flight geography

description.en: UAS.STS-02.020(8)(b) requires an active system that prevents the aircraft breaching the flight geography, and UAS.STS-02.040(1)(a) requires the pilot to set the programmable flight volume to keep it inside. When the aircraft is out of visual line of sight it must follow a pre-programmed trajectory. Program the volume and the trajectory from the site map for each flight and check them on the ground station before take-off.

evidenceHint.en: Programmed flight volume and trajectory for each STS-02 flight, compared with the site's flight geography

text.en: Enter the flight geography from the site map into the aircraft's programmable volume.
Program the trajectory the aircraft follows while out of visual line of sight.
Compare the programmed volume and trajectory with the site map on the ground station.
Save the programmed volume with the flight record.

title.en: Verify STS-02 flight termination, programmable volume and remote identification before each flight

description.en: Before each STS-02 operation UAS.STS-02.040(1)(b) requires the pilot to verify that the means to terminate the flight and the programmable operational volume function are operational, and that direct remote identification is active and up to date. Make all three mandatory items on the STS-02 pre-flight checklist and ground the aircraft if any one fails.

evidenceHint.en: STS-02 pre-flight checklist entries for each flight recording the termination, programmable volume and remote identification checks

text.en: Run the manufacturer's check of the flight termination means.
Confirm the programmable operational volume function is active and holds the set volume.
Confirm remote identification is active and broadcasts the correct operator number.
Record all three results before take-off and ground the aircraft if any fails.

title.en: Plan STS-02 launch, recovery and range so the aircraft stays in reach of the pilot

description.en: UAS.STS-02.020(4) requires the aircraft to be in sight of the pilot during launch and recovery unless recovery results from an emergency termination. Without airspace observers, UAS.STS-02.020(5) limits the aircraft to 1 km from the pilot. Plan each launch and recovery point in view of the pilot's position, and check the trajectory never takes an observer-free flight beyond 1 km.

evidenceHint.en: Flight plan showing launch and recovery points in view of the pilot and the maximum planned distance from the pilot

text.en: Place the launch and recovery points where the pilot has a clear view of them.
Measure the planned trajectory's greatest distance from the pilot's position.
Keep that distance within 1 km when no airspace observer is used.
Record the maximum distance actually flown in the flight log.

title.en: Review STS-02 flight records for flight geography breaches and termination events

description.en: Each quarter review STS-02 tracks and events: any approach to the flight geography limit should show the contingency procedure applied, any exit from the operational volume should show flight termination triggered, and any termination should be in the occurrence log. Check also that every aircraft flown was flagged as C6-eligible and listed in the declaration.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly STS-02 review of tracks and events, with the procedure applied to each and findings raised

text.en: Pull the tracks and event logs for the quarter's STS-02 flights.
Find every approach to or breach of the flight geography and the action taken.
Check every flight termination is recorded in the occurrence log.
Check each aircraft flown was C6-eligible and listed in the declaration.
Raise findings with owners for every gap.

templates.title: STS-02 airspace observers and visibility
templates.description: STS-02 flights beyond visual line of sight use airspace observers placed to cover the operational volume and surrounding airspace within the scenario's distance limits, with robust communication to the pilot, a flight visibility above 5 km and a briefing on the planned path and timing.
templates.objective: To ensure STS-02 airspace observers are placed, linked, briefed and working within the distance and visibility limits so manned traffic is seen in time.
templates.successCriteria:
Every STS-02 flight with observers kept the aircraft within 2 km of the pilot and 1 km of the nearest observer, with each observer within 1 km of the pilot.
The observers' zones covered the operational volume and surrounding airspace with no gaps and no terrain obstruction.
Flight visibility above 5 km was recorded from the pilot's and each observer's position before take-off.
Communication with each observer was tested before flight, and each observer was briefed on the path, timing and their duties.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the observer deployment plans, visibility checks, communication checks and briefing records for STS-02 flights in the period.
Obtain the operations manual limits for observer visibility and distance.
Obtain the flight tracks and the observers' positions for sampled flights.

Analysis:
Measure on each sampled plan the distances between the aircraft, the pilot and the observers and compare them with the 2 km and 1 km limits in UAS.STS-02.020(6).
Check the observers' coverage zones for gaps and for terrain or obstacles blocking their view.
Check that visibility above 5 km was recorded from every position before take-off, and that the conditions recorded support it.
Check that a communication test and a briefing were recorded for each observer before each flight.
Compare the deployment with the limits the operations manual sets.

Output:
A list of sampled flights exceeding a distance limit or with gaps in observer coverage.
A list of flights without a visibility, communication or briefing record.
Any deployment outside the operations manual limits.

title.en: Determine the number and placement of airspace observers along each STS-02 flight path

description.en: When observers are used, UAS.STS-02.020(6) requires them to cover the operational volume and surrounding airspace, with the aircraft no further than 2 km from the pilot and 1 km from the nearest observer, and no observer more than 1 km from the pilot. UAS.STS-02.030(10) adds that there must be no gaps between observers' zones and no terrain obstruction for any of them. Plan positions on the map and measure each distance.

evidenceHint.en: Observer deployment plan per site with positions, coverage zones and measured distances to the pilot and the aircraft path

text.en: Mark the pilot's position and the planned trajectory on the site map.
Place observers so each part of the path is within 1 km of one of them.
Check each observer is within 1 km of the pilot and the path within 2 km of the pilot.
Check each observer's view for terrain or obstacles that would block it.
Confirm the coverage zones join with no gaps along the whole path.

title.en: Establish robust communication between the STS-02 remote pilot and each airspace observer

description.en: UAS.STS-02.020(6)(e) requires robust and effective communication between the pilot and the observers, and UAS.STS-02.030(10)(b) requires it to be verified before each operation, together with any means the observers use to know the aircraft's position. Choose a primary and a backup means, agree calls for traffic, hazards and deviations, and test both at the observers' actual positions.

evidenceHint.en: Communication plan with primary and backup means and agreed calls, and the pre-flight test record for each observer

text.en: Choose a primary communication means and a backup for each observer.
Agree the calls for traffic sighted, hazard, loss of sight and stop.
Test both means from each observer's position before every operation.
Check any position display the observers use is working and shows the aircraft.
Record each test result and delay take-off until every link works.

title.en: Check flight visibility above 5 km from every pilot and observer position before take-off

description.en: UAS.STS-02.020(3) requires a minimum flight visibility of more than 5 km. GM1 reads this as the shortest distance, in all directions, at which unlighted objects can be seen by day from the pilot's and each observer's position, and asks the operator to consider sun glare, obstacles, cloud ceiling and smoke. Check and record it from each position before take-off and again if conditions change.

evidenceHint.en: Visibility check from each position for each STS-02 flight, with the reference features used and the conditions noted

text.en: Pick reference features more than 5 km away in several directions from each position.
Confirm each position can see them, noting sun glare, haze, smoke or low cloud.
Record the visibility judgement from the pilot and each observer before take-off.
Stop or delay the flight if visibility from any position falls to 5 km or less.

title.en: Brief STS-02 airspace observers on the flight path, timing and their duties

description.en: UAS.STS-02.030(10)(c) requires observers to be briefed on the intended path of the aircraft and its timing. UAS.STS-02.050 sets their duties: scan the airspace around the aircraft for manned traffic, keep aware of the aircraft's position by direct sight or electronic means, and alert the pilot to hazards and help avoid them. The pilot in turn tells observers in good time of any deviation from the path.

evidenceHint.en: Observer briefing record for each STS-02 flight covering path, timing, duties and the deviation calls agreed

text.en: Show each observer the path, the timing and the part of the airspace they cover.
Restate the observer's duties to scan, track the aircraft and alert the pilot.
Agree how the pilot will announce deviations from the planned path.
Record the briefing and each observer's confirmation before take-off.

title.en: Review each STS-02 observer deployment against the operations manual limits

description.en: UAS.STS-02.030(10)(b)(i) requires the visibility and planned distance of each observer to be within the limits the operations manual sets.
