Each month sample STS-02 flights flown with observers and compare the recorded positions, distances, visibility, communication tests and briefings with the regulation's limits and the manual's own, then raise findings for any departure.

evidenceHint.en: Monthly review of sampled STS-02 observer deployments against the regulation and manual limits, with findings

text.en: Select a sample of STS-02 flights flown with airspace observers.
Compare recorded distances with the 2 km and 1 km limits and the manual's limits.
Check the visibility, communication and briefing records exist for each observer.
Raise findings for each departure and update the manual if a limit proved unworkable.

templates.title: Operational risk assessment under Article 11 (SORA or PDRA)
templates.description: Every operation flown under an operational authorisation, and every operation an LUC holder authorises itself, rests on a written Article 11 risk assessment, made with SORA or with a predefined risk assessment that fits, and kept current as the operation changes.
templates.objective: To ensure every authorised or self-authorised specific operation rests on a current Article 11 risk assessment whose mitigations are reviewed and kept adequate.
templates.successCriteria:
Every operation flown under an authorisation or an LUC privilege maps to one dated risk assessment that names its method: SORA 2.5, or a PDRA with its number and edition.
Each SORA assessment records the operation description, the final ground and residual air risk classes, the SAIL, the containment requirements and each operational safety objective with its robustness.
Each PDRA-based assessment shows the operation stays within the PDRA's limits and applies every mitigation it lists.
Each assessment was reviewed in the last twelve months and again after any change to the aircraft, area, airspace, crew or procedures.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the register of operation types flown under an operational authorisation or an LUC privilege in the period, with the risk assessment each relies on.
Obtain each risk assessment with its version history, and for PDRA-based operations the PDRA number and edition used.
Obtain the record of mitigation reviews made under UAS.SPEC.010 and the change log for aircraft, areas, crews and procedures.

Analysis:
Trace a sample of flights from the flight log to an operation type and to the risk assessment in force on the flight date.
For each sampled SORA assessment, check that every step from the operation description to the safety portfolio is completed and that the SAIL follows from the ground and air risk classes recorded.
For each sampled PDRA-based operation, compare the flown operation with the PDRA's applicability limits and confirm each listed mitigation has an owner and evidence.
Compare the change log with the assessment history and identify changes that were not followed by a reassessment.
Confirm security and privacy were assessed separately where a PDRA was used, since a PDRA addresses safety only.

Output:
A table of sampled flights, the assessment and method each relied on, and whether it was current on the flight date.
A list of assessments with missing steps, unsupported robustness claims or a SAIL that does not follow from the recorded risk classes.
A list of changes made without a reassessment.

title.en: Choose SORA or a predefined risk assessment for each planned operation type

description.en: Decide, for each operation type the operator intends to fly under an authorisation or an LUC privilege, whether a predefined risk assessment (PDRA) covers it or a full SORA is needed. The current PDRAs are G01 v1.3, G02 v1.2, G03 v1.1 and S01 v1.2 (ED Decision 2023/012/R) and S02 v1.1 (ED Decision 2022/002/R). A PDRA addresses safety only, so plan a separate assessment of security and privacy. Record the choice and the reason for it.

evidenceHint.en: Operation-type register naming, for each type, the method chosen (SORA 2.5 or a PDRA with number and edition) and why

text.en: List every operation type the operator plans to fly in the specific category outside a standard scenario.
Compare each type with the applicability limits of PDRA-G01, G02, G03, S01 and S02.
Record the PDRA number and edition for each type a PDRA fully covers.
Mark every type no PDRA fully covers for a full SORA 2.5 assessment.
Note for each PDRA-based type how security and privacy will be assessed separately.

title.en: Document the operation and determine its ground and air risk classes under SORA

description.en: Complete the first six SORA steps for each operation that needs a full assessment: document the concept of operations, determine the intrinsic ground risk class, apply any ground risk mitigations to reach the final ground risk class, determine the initial air risk class, apply strategic mitigations to reach the residual air risk class, and set the tactical mitigation performance requirements. Record the population density data, airspace and buffers used, as Article 11(2) requires them in the operation description.

evidenceHint.en: SORA working file with the concept of operations, the population and airspace data used, the final ground risk class, the residual air risk class and the tactical mitigation requirements

text.en: Write the concept of operations: activities, area, airspace, aircraft, crew and planned buffers.
Determine the intrinsic ground risk class from the aircraft dimension and the overflown population density.
Apply only the ground risk mitigations you can evidence and record the final ground risk class.
Determine the initial air risk class from the operational airspace and apply any strategic mitigations.
Record the residual air risk class and the tactical mitigation requirements it sets.

title.en: Derive the SAIL, containment requirements and safety objectives for the operation

description.en: Finish the SORA: assign the SAIL from the final ground and residual air risk classes, determine the containment requirements for the adjacent ground area and airspace, and list each operational safety objective with the robustness the SAIL requires. Assemble the comprehensive safety portfolio that shows how each objective is met, so the assessment proposes mitigations with a robustness the competent authority can judge, as Article 11(1)(e) asks.

evidenceHint.en: Completed SORA assessment showing the SAIL, containment requirements and each operational safety objective with its required robustness and the evidence that meets it

text.en: Assign the SAIL from the final ground risk class and the residual air risk class.
Determine the containment requirements for the adjacent ground area and airspace.
List each operational safety objective with the robustness level the SAIL requires.
Attach the evidence that meets each objective at the required robustness.
Version, date and approve the assessment before it supports any application or self-authorisation.

title.en: Reassess the operational risk whenever the operation, aircraft or area changes

description.en: A risk assessment is valid only for the operation it describes. Before flying a changed operation, reassess it: a new aircraft or payload, a new area or a different population density, a different airspace, a change of crew composition or a revised procedure can all move the risk classes. For an operation under an authorisation, a significant change also triggers an application for an updated authorisation; for an LUC holder, reassess before self-authorising the changed operation.

evidenceHint.en: Change records each showing the assessment reviewed, the outcome and, where the risk classes moved, the new assessment version

text.en: Record each proposed change to aircraft, payload, area, airspace, crew or procedures before it takes effect.
Check whether the change moves the ground risk class, the air risk class or the SAIL.
Revise the assessment and its mitigations where the risk moves, and version it.
Flag changes that are significant for the authorisation so an updated authorisation can be applied for.
Hold the changed operation until the revised assessment is approved.

title.en: Review the adequacy of each operation's mitigations against flight and occurrence data

description.en: UAS.SPEC.010 requires the operator to evaluate regularly whether its mitigations remain adequate and to update them where necessary. Once a year, and after any serious occurrence, compare each assessment's mitigations with what flight logs, occurrence reports and maintenance records show actually happened, and decide whether any mitigation or robustness claim needs to change.

evidenceHint.en: Annual mitigation review record per assessment, listing the data reviewed, the conclusion on each mitigation and the updates made

text.en: Collect the year's flight logs, occurrence reports and maintenance findings for each operation type.
Compare each mitigation with the events that tested it, such as fly-aways, link losses or intrusions.
Decide whether each mitigation is still adequate at the robustness the assessment claims.
Update the assessment and the procedures where a mitigation fell short.
Record the review, its conclusions and the date of the next one.

templates.title: Operational authorisation application and scope
templates.description: The operator obtains its operational authorisation from the competent authority of its State of registration before flying, with a complete application built on its Article 11 assessment, and turns the scope and conditions it is granted into its own procedures.
templates.objective: To ensure no authorised operation starts before its authorisation is issued, and that each application gives the competent authority everything it needs to judge the risk.
templates.successCriteria:
Every operational authorisation was applied for to the competent authority of the State of registration and was issued before the first flight it covers.
Each application carried the registration number, the accountable manager, the risk assessment, the mitigation list, an operations manual where needed and the insurance confirmation.
Each application included a signed statement that the operation complies with Union and national rules on privacy, data protection, liability, insurance, security and the environment.
Every operation in controlled airspace has an agreed coordination procedure with the airspace service provider.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain each operational authorisation application submitted, with its attachments and submission date, and each authorisation or refusal received.
Obtain the Article 12(2)(c) compliance statement submitted with each application and the evidence behind it.
Obtain the coordination procedures agreed with air navigation service providers for operations in controlled airspace.
Obtain the flight log for the period.

Analysis:
Check each application against the six elements UAS.SPEC.030(3) requires and note any missing or thin element, in particular a mitigation list too vague to judge.
Compare the date of the first flight under each authorisation with the issue date of the authorisation.
Read each compliance statement and confirm it was signed by an accountable person and backed by evidence for each subject it covers.
Identify flights in controlled airspace and confirm each was covered by a coordination procedure.
For each refusal, confirm the reasons given were recorded and addressed before reapplying.

Output:
An application-by-application completeness table against UAS.SPEC.030(3) and Article 12(2)(c).
A list of flights made before the authorisation covering them was issued.
A list of controlled-airspace operations without an agreed coordination procedure.

title.en: Assemble the operational authorisation application from the Article 11 assessment

description.en: Build the application to the competent authority of the State of registration from the approved risk assessment. UAS.SPEC.030(3) requires the operator's registration number, the name of the accountable manager, the operational risk assessment, the list of proposed mitigations with enough detail for the authority to judge them, an operations manual when the risk and complexity require one, and a confirmation that insurance will be in place where Union or national law requires it.

evidenceHint.en: Application pack with a checklist showing each UAS.SPEC.030(3) element present, and the submission receipt

text.en: Confirm the application goes to the competent authority of the State of registration.
Attach the approved risk assessment and the operator's registration number.
Name the accountable manager and list each mitigation with enough detail to judge its adequacy.
Attach the operations manual where the risk and complexity of the operation call for one.
Add the insurance confirmation where Union or national law requires cover, then file the submission receipt.

title.en: Sign the Article 12 statement of compliance with privacy, liability, insurance, security and environment rules

description.en: Article 12(2)(c) makes the authorisation conditional on a statement that the intended operation complies with Union and national rules on privacy, data protection, liability, insurance, security and environmental protection. Gather the evidence for each subject from the people who own it, so the statement is signed knowingly rather than as a formality, and keep the evidence with the application.

evidenceHint.en: Signed Article 12(2)(c) statement with an evidence index covering each of the six subjects

text.en: Ask the data protection officer to confirm the privacy and data protection position and attach it.
Obtain the insurance certificate and the liability position for each State of operation.
Confirm the security requirements of the operating area and how the operation meets them.
Record any environmental condition that applies, such as protected areas or noise limits.
Have the accountable manager sign the statement once every subject has evidence attached.

title.en: Agree an airspace coordination procedure for authorised operations in controlled airspace

description.en: UAS.SPEC.040(1)(b) lets the competent authority issue an authorisation only when a procedure is in place for coordination with the relevant airspace service provider if any part of the operation is in controlled airspace. Agree the procedure in writing with the air navigation service provider before applying, covering how and when the operator notifies, how clearance is obtained and how the operation is stopped on request.

evidenceHint.en: Written coordination procedure or letter of agreement with the air navigation service provider, with contact points and notification steps

text.en: Identify every planned operation that enters controlled airspace, even in part.
Contact the responsible air navigation service provider and agree the coordination method.
Write down notification timings, clearance steps, contact points and how a stop request is handled.
Attach the agreed procedure to the authorisation application.
Brief remote pilots on the procedure before any operation in that airspace.

title.en: Hold authorised operations until the authorisation is issued and its scope is confirmed

description.en: UAS.SPEC.030(1) requires the authorisation before the operation starts. Make the flight-release process check that an issued authorisation covers the planned operation: its type, locations, aircraft, crew competency and conditions. If the authority refuses, it must give reasons under Article 12(3); record them and revise the assessment or application before trying again, rather than flying under another basis.

evidenceHint.en: Flight release records showing the authorisation reference checked, and a log of any refusal with its reasons and the response

text.en: Add an authorisation reference field to the flight release and make it mandatory.
Check before release that the authorisation covers the operation type, location and aircraft.
Block release for any operation whose authorisation is pending, expired or refused.
Record the reasons given for any refusal and the changes made in response.

title.en: Reconcile the issued authorisation against the application before the first flight

description.en: An authorisation details its own scope, conditions, required competency, technical features, locations, mitigations and the records and extra reportable events the authority expects (Article 12(4)). These can differ from what was applied for. Compare the issued text with the application line by line and carry every difference into the procedures, crew briefings and flight-release checks before the first flight.

evidenceHint.en: Reconciliation sheet listing each authorisation term, whether it matches the application, and where it is now reflected in procedures

text.en: List every scope item, condition, mitigation and location the issued authorisation states.
Compare each one with what the application proposed and flag the differences.
Note any extra reportable events or records the authorisation requires beyond Regulation 376/2014.
Update procedures, briefings and release checks for each difference found.
Sign off the reconciliation before the first flight under the authorisation.

templates.title: Authorisation conditions, changes and validity
templates.description: The operator keeps a register of what each authorisation allows and requires, applies for an updated authorisation before any significant change, tracks its duration, never treats it as transferable, and acknowledges any revocation or surrender at once.
templates.objective: To ensure the operator always flies within a live authorisation whose conditions it can show it meets, and that changes, expiry and revocation are handled before they bite.
templates.successCriteria:
Each authorisation has a conditions register listing its scope, limitations, mitigations, locations, required records and extra reportable events.
Every significant change to an operation or its mitigations was preceded by an application for an updated authorisation.
No flight took place under an authorisation that had expired, been revoked or been surrendered.
Every revocation or surrender was acknowledged to the competent authority in digital form without delay.
No authorisation was used by a legal entity other than the one it was issued to.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain every operational authorisation held in the period with its duration, conditions and any amendments.
Obtain the conditions register for each authorisation and the change log for operations and mitigations.
Obtain any revocation or surrender notices and the acknowledgements returned.
Obtain the flight log and records of the operator's legal identity, such as company registration changes.

Analysis:
Compare each conditions register with the authorisation text and note any term the register omits.
Read the change log and decide for each change whether it was significant to the operation or its mitigations; for each significant one, confirm an updated authorisation was applied for before the change took effect.
Compare flight dates with each authorisation's duration and any revocation or surrender date.
Check the date of each digital acknowledgement against the date of the revocation or surrender.
Confirm the legal entity named on each authorisation is the one flying under it.
Sample flights and test them against the register's conditions.

Output:
A list of register gaps against each authorisation's text.
A list of significant changes made without an updated authorisation, and flights outside a live authorisation.
A statement on the timeliness of each acknowledgement and on any use of an authorisation by another entity.

title.en: Build a register of every condition and limitation the authorisation sets

description.en: Turn each authorisation into a register the operator can check against: its scope, the operational limitations and conditions, the required competency of remote pilots, the technical features of the aircraft, the mitigations the operator must apply, the authorised locations, and the documents, records and reportable events Article 12(4) lists. Give each line an owner who keeps it true.

evidenceHint.en: Conditions register per authorisation, one line per term with its owner and the evidence that shows it is met

text.en: Copy each scope item, limitation and condition from the authorisation into the register.
Add the required pilot competency, aircraft technical features and authorised locations.
List the mitigations the authorisation requires and the records and extra reportable events it names.
Assign an owner to each line and name the evidence that shows it is met.
Record the authorisation's start date and the duration the competent authority stated.

title.en: Add a significant-change check that decides whether an updated authorisation is needed

description.en: UAS.SPEC.030(2) requires an application for an updated authorisation for any significant change to the operation or to the mitigations listed in it. Add a step to the operator's change process that compares every proposed change with the conditions register and decides, with a recorded reason, whether it is significant. A significant change waits for the updated authorisation.

evidenceHint.en: Change-assessment procedure and completed change records, each with a significance decision, the reason and any updated application filed

text.en: Write criteria for a significant change, covering aircraft, area, airspace, crew, procedures and mitigations.
Route every proposed change through a comparison with the conditions register.
Record whether each change is significant and the reason for the decision.
Apply for an updated authorisation before any significant change takes effect.
Keep the changed operation on hold until the updated authorisation is received.

title.en: Apply afresh when the authorised operation passes to a different legal entity

description.en: UAS.SPEC.070 says an operational authorisation is not transferable. When the operation moves to another company, after a sale, a merger, a restructuring or a new subsidiary, the receiving entity cannot fly under the old authorisation. Make the corporate change process flag this early, so the new entity registers and applies for its own authorisation before it takes the operation over.

evidenceHint.en: Corporate change checklist entry showing the authorisation flagged, and the new entity's registration and application records

text.en: Add the operational authorisation to the checklist for any sale, merger or restructuring.
Confirm which legal entity the authorisation was issued to and who will fly after the change.
Have the receiving entity register as an operator and apply for its own authorisation.
Stop flights by the receiving entity until its own authorisation is issued.

title.en: Track each authorisation's duration and act on revocation or surrender without delay

description.en: UAS.SPEC.080 has the competent authority state each authorisation's duration, keeps it valid only while the operator stays compliant, and requires a digital acknowledgement returned without delay on revocation or surrender. Track the expiry date so renewal is applied for in time, and keep a ready procedure for stopping operations and acknowledging a revocation or surrender the day it happens.

evidenceHint.en: Authorisation tracker with expiry dates and renewal actions, and the dated digital acknowledgement for any revocation or surrender

text.en: Enter each authorisation's expiry date and set reminders well before it.
Apply for renewal early enough that operations do not lapse.
On revocation or surrender, stop every operation that relied on the authorisation the same day.
Return the digital acknowledgement to the competent authority without delay and file a copy.

title.en: Spot-check a quarter's authorised flights against the authorisation's conditions

description.en: Each quarter, sample flights made under each authorisation and test them against the conditions register: location, airspace, aircraft, crew competency, mitigations applied, and the records and reportable events the authorisation requires. A gap found here is cheaper than one found in the authority's oversight, which can end the authorisation under UAS.SPEC.080(2).

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly self-check worksheet listing flights sampled, each condition tested, findings raised and their owners

text.en: Select a sample of flights under each authorisation from the quarter's flight log.
Test each sampled flight against every line of the conditions register.
Confirm the records and extra reportable events the authorisation requires were produced.
Raise a finding for each breach with an owner and a due date.
Report the results and open findings to the accountable manager.

templates.title: Operations manual and emergency response plan for authorised operations
templates.description: Where the risk and complexity of an authorised operation require it, the operator keeps an operations manual and an emergency response plan at the robustness its risk assessment claims, validates the procedures in them and amends both when the operation changes.
templates.objective: To ensure the procedures an authorised operation's risk assessment relies on are written down, validated, known by the crew and kept in step with the authorisation.
templates.successCriteria:
For each authorised operation a recorded decision states whether an operations manual is required, with the reason taken from the risk assessment.
Each required manual holds normal, contingency and emergency procedures at the robustness the risk assessment claims.
An emergency response plan covers escalation limits, alerting conditions, the criteria that define an emergency and each person's duties.
The contingency and emergency procedures were validated by flight test or representative simulation before use.
The manual was amended within a month of each change to the authorisation or its mitigations.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the operations manual and emergency response plan for each authorised operation, with their revision history and distribution lists.
Obtain the risk assessment each relies on and the authorisation it supports.
Obtain the records of flight tests, simulations and emergency exercises used to validate the procedures.
Obtain crew acknowledgements of the current revision.

Analysis:
Compare the procedures the risk assessment relies on with the manual's contents and identify any that are claimed but not written.
Read the emergency response plan for the four elements: limiting escalation, alerting authorities and organisations, emergency criteria and duties.
Trace each contingency and emergency procedure to a validation record and judge whether a simulation used was representative.
Compare the revision dates with the change dates of the authorisation and mitigations.
Sample crew members and confirm each acknowledged the current revision.

Output:
A procedure-by-procedure table of manual coverage and validation status.
A list of emergency response plan elements missing or untested.
A list of crew members working from an outdated revision.

title.en: Decide whether the authorised operation needs an operations manual and to what robustness

description.en: UAS.SPEC.030(3)(e) asks for an operations manual when the risk and complexity of the operation require one. Use the risk assessment to decide: the operational safety objectives on procedures and training, and the robustness the SAIL demands, tell you whether a manual is needed and how much assurance it must carry. EASA's guidance on UAS.SPEC.030(3)(e) offers a manual template. Record the decision and its reasoning.

evidenceHint.en: Recorded decision per authorised operation on whether an operations manual is needed, citing the risk assessment and the robustness required

text.en: Read the risk assessment's operational safety objectives on procedures, training and crew.
Note the robustness level the SAIL requires for each of those objectives.
Decide whether an operations manual is needed and record the reason.
Choose the manual structure, using EASA's template where it fits.

title.en: Write the authorised operation's normal, contingency and emergency procedures

description.en: Write the procedures the risk assessment relies on into the operations manual: normal procedures for planning, pre-flight, flight and post-flight; contingency procedures for degraded conditions such as a weak link or a breach of the flight geography; emergency procedures for loss of control or a fly-away. Add the organisation, crew roles, training and maintenance chapters the operation needs, and keep each procedure traceable to the mitigation it delivers.

evidenceHint.en: Operations manual revision with normal, contingency and emergency procedures, each referenced to the mitigation in the risk assessment it delivers

text.en: Write the normal procedures from flight planning through post-flight checks.
Write contingency procedures for each degraded condition the risk assessment identifies.
Write emergency procedures for loss of control, fly-away and loss of containment.
Add the organisation, crew roles, training and maintenance chapters the operation needs.
Reference each procedure to the mitigation in the risk assessment it delivers.

title.en: Draft the emergency response plan for authorised operations

description.en: Write an emergency response plan the crew can act on under stress. It sets out how to limit the escalating effects of an emergency, the conditions under which authorities and organisations are alerted and how to reach them, the criteria that identify an emergency, and the duties of the remote pilot and every other person with an essential task. Include contact details valid for each operating area.

evidenceHint.en: Approved emergency response plan with escalation actions, alerting conditions and contacts, emergency criteria and named duties

text.en: Define the criteria that turn an abnormal situation into an emergency.
Write the immediate actions that limit escalation, such as flight termination or area clearance.
List the conditions for alerting authorities and organisations and their contact details per area.
Assign duties to the remote pilot and each other person with an essential task.
Approve the plan and attach it to the operations manual.

title.en: Validate the contingency and emergency procedures by flight test or simulation and exercise the plan

description.en: Show that the contingency and emergency procedures work before relying on them, by dedicated flight tests or by a simulation representative of the real aircraft and conditions, at the assurance the risk assessment claims. Then exercise the emergency response plan with the crew and, where possible, the services it names. Record what worked, what did not and what changed.

evidenceHint.en: Validation records for each procedure (flight test or simulation, with representativeness noted) and the emergency exercise report with actions taken

text.en: List each contingency and emergency procedure that needs validation.
Validate each one by a dedicated flight test or a representative simulation and record the result.
Run an emergency exercise with the crew, using a realistic scenario from the risk assessment.
Record the findings and update the procedures or the plan where they fell short.

title.en: Amend and redistribute the operations manual when the authorisation or mitigations change

description.en: A manual that lags the authorisation trains the crew on the wrong limits. Treat the operations manual and emergency response plan as controlled documents: revise them after every change to the authorisation, the risk assessment or the mitigations, record each revision, distribute it to everyone who needs it and collect acknowledgements, and withdraw superseded copies.

evidenceHint.en: Revision history of the manual and plan, distribution list and crew acknowledgements of the current revision

text.en: Check the manual and plan against each change to the authorisation, assessment or mitigations.
Revise the affected sections and record the revision number and date.
Distribute the revision to everyone on the distribution list.
Collect acknowledgements and chase anyone who has not confirmed the current revision.
Withdraw superseded copies from field kits and shared drives.

templates.title: LUC application, terms of approval and privileges
templates.description: The organisation applies for a light UAS operator certificate as a legal person with a complete application, holds the terms of approval on file, maps every operation to the privileges they grant, and treats the certificate as non-transferable except through an approved ownership change.
templates.objective: To ensure the organisation's LUC application is complete and that every operation it runs on the LUC's privileges falls within the terms of approval the authority granted.
templates.successCriteria:
The LUC application was made by a legal person and contained the management system description, the named responsible personnel and the verification statement.
The current terms of approval are on file and state the operator identification, privileges, authorised types of operation, area or airspace and any limitations.
Every operation type run under the LUC maps to a privilege and an authorised type in the terms.
No change of ownership took effect without the competent authority's prior approval.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the LUC application and any amendment applications, with their attachments and dates.
Obtain the LUC with its terms of approval and any amendments.
Obtain the register of operation types run under the LUC's privileges in the period.
Obtain records of any ownership or corporate change and the competent authority's approvals.

Analysis:
Check the application against UAS.LUC.010(2): the management system and safety management system description, the named personnel including the person authorising operations, and the signed verification statement.
Read the terms of approval for the five elements UAS.LUC.050(2) lists and note any left open.
Map each operation type run under the LUC to a privilege and an authorised type of operation, and identify any that map to neither.
Compare the dates of any ownership change with the date of the competent authority's approval.

Output:
A completeness statement on the application and the terms of approval.
A table mapping each operation type to the privilege and authorised type it relies on, with any unmapped type highlighted.
A statement on whether any ownership change took effect before approval.

title.en: Confirm LUC eligibility and decide which privileges to apply for

description.en: Only a legal person may apply for an LUC (UAS.LUC.010(1)). Decide which privileges the organisation needs. EASA's guidance describes self-authorising operations based on a standard scenario without a declaration, and operations based on a PDRA, on variants of a standard scenario, or within a type of activity already performed, without prior approval. The authority may widen privileges gradually as a safety record builds. Record the privileges sought and why.

evidenceHint.en: Eligibility record naming the applying legal entity and a privileges plan listing each privilege sought and the operations it would cover

text.en: Confirm the applicant is a legal person and record its registration details.
List the operation types the organisation expects to run in the specific category.
Match each operation type to the privilege that would let the organisation authorise it.
Record which privileges to request now and which to seek later as the safety record builds.

title.en: Compile the LUC application with the management system description and named personnel

description.en: Prepare the application UAS.LUC.010(2) requires: a description of the management system, including the organisational structure and the safety management system; the names of the responsible personnel, including the person responsible for authorising operations; and a statement that all documentation submitted was verified by the applicant and found to comply. Use the same pack for any later amendment application.

evidenceHint.en: LUC application pack with the management system description, the list of named responsible personnel and the signed verification statement, plus the submission receipt

text.en: Describe the organisational structure and the safety management system.
Name the responsible personnel, including the person who will authorise operations.
Verify every document in the pack against the requirements of Part C.
Sign the statement that the documentation was verified and found to comply.
Submit the application to the competent authority and file the receipt.

title.en: File the LUC terms of approval and map every operation type to them

description.en: When the LUC is issued, its terms of approval state the operator identification, its privileges, the authorised types of operation, the authorised area, zone or class of airspace, and any special limitations or conditions (UAS.LUC.050(2)). Keep the current terms where operations staff can read them, and maintain a map from every operation type the organisation runs to the privilege and authorised type it relies on.

evidenceHint.en: Current terms of approval on file and an operation-type map showing, for each type, the privilege, authorised type, area and limitations that apply

text.en: File the issued LUC and its terms of approval where operations staff can read them.
List each privilege, authorised type of operation, area or airspace and limitation the terms state.
Map every operation type the organisation runs to one privilege and one authorised type.
Flag any operation type that maps to nothing and stop it until it is covered.

title.en: Obtain approval before any change of ownership and never transfer the LUC otherwise

description.en: UAS.LUC.075 makes an LUC non-transferable except for a change to the ownership of the organisation that the competent authority has approved under UAS.LUC.070. Put the LUC on the checklist for any sale, merger or restructuring so the authority's prior approval is sought in good time, and so no other entity ever operates under the certificate.

evidenceHint.en: Corporate change checklist with the LUC item, the request for prior approval and the competent authority's decision

text.en: Add the LUC to the checklist for any ownership change, sale, merger or restructuring.
Request the competent authority's prior approval for an ownership change before it takes effect.
Confirm no other legal entity operates under the LUC at any time.
File the authority's decision with the LUC records.

title.en: Review the LUC privileges used against the terms of approval each year

description.en: Once a year, compare what the organisation actually authorised itself to do with what its terms of approval allow. Operations that crept outside the authorised types, areas or limitations need to stop or be brought within an amended LUC, which is applied for under UAS.LUC.010(2) and needs prior approval as a change to the terms under UAS.LUC.070.

evidenceHint.en: Annual privileges review comparing self-authorised operations with the terms of approval, and any amendment application made

text.en: Extract the year's self-authorised operations from the internal authorisation records.
Compare each one with the privileges, types, areas and limitations in the terms of approval.
Stop any operation found outside the terms until it is covered.
Apply for an amendment where the organisation needs wider terms.
Report the review to the accountable manager.

templates.title: Accountable manager, safety policy and safety personnel
templates.description: The LUC holder's safety management system is sized to the organisation and led by an accountable manager with clear lines of responsibility, a safety policy with objectives, appointed key safety personnel and continuing safety training and communication.
templates.objective: To ensure the LUC holder's safety management system has an accountable leader, a stated policy and objectives, the people to execute them, and staff who know their part.
templates.successCriteria:
A documented assessment explains how the safety management system is sized to the organisation's size, activities and hazards.
An accountable manager is nominated in writing with authority over every activity, and responsibilities are mapped for each role.
A signed safety policy and dated safety objectives with measures exist and are known to staff.
The safety manager and other key safety personnel are appointed in writing, with no conflict between the accountable manager and safety manager roles.
Every member of staff completed safety training in the last twelve months.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the safety management system description, the organisation chart and the role descriptions.
Obtain the accountable manager's nomination, the safety policy and the safety objectives with their measures and results.
Obtain the appointment letters of the safety manager and other key safety personnel.
Obtain safety training records and safety communications issued in the period.

Analysis:
Read the sizing assessment and judge whether the system's scope matches the organisation's size, the nature of its operations and its hazards.
Confirm the accountable manager's authority covers every activity and that each role's responsibilities and accountabilities are written.
Check that the safety manager role is not held by the accountable manager where the safety manager also acts as compliance monitoring manager.
Compare safety objectives with results and note objectives with no measure or no reported result.
Sample staff and confirm they completed safety training and can state the safety policy's main commitments.

Output:
A statement on whether the system is proportionate to the organisation.
A list of missing appointments, conflicting roles or unwritten responsibilities.
A list of objectives without measures and staff without current safety training.

title.en: Scope the LUC holder's safety management system to its organisation and operations

description.en: UAS.LUC.030(1) asks for a safety management system that corresponds to the size of the organisation and the nature and complexity of its activities, taking account of their hazards and risks. Write down what the organisation does, how many people and sites it has and which hazards dominate, and from that decide how elaborate each part of the system needs to be. If the organisation holds other certificates under Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, decide whether to integrate the systems.

evidenceHint.en: Sizing assessment describing the organisation, its operations and hazards, and the resulting scope of each part of the safety management system

text.en: Describe the organisation's size, sites, fleet and the types of operation it runs.
List the main hazards those operations carry.
Decide how elaborate each part of the safety management system needs to be.
Decide whether to integrate with the safety management system of any other 2018/1139 certificate held.

title.en: Name the accountable manager and define lines of responsibility and accountability

description.en: Nominate in writing an accountable manager with the authority to make sure every activity is performed to the applicable standards and that the organisation stays compliant with its management system and the LUC manual. Then write clear lines of responsibility and accountability through the organisation, so that for every safety task it is plain who does it and who answers for it.

evidenceHint.en: Signed nomination of the accountable manager stating their authority, and an organisation chart with written responsibilities and accountabilities per role

text.en: Nominate the accountable manager in writing and state the authority the role carries.
Draw the organisation chart down to every role with a safety task.
Write each role's responsibilities and to whom it is accountable.
Have each role holder sign their role description.

title.en: Publish the LUC safety policy with measurable safety objectives

description.en: Write a safety policy signed by the accountable manager that states the organisation's safety commitments, including how it treats safety reports. Set safety objectives that follow from it and can be measured, such as occurrence rates, report closure times or training completion, and state how and how often each is measured. Publish both to every member of staff.

evidenceHint.en: Signed safety policy and a list of safety objectives, each with its measure, target and reporting frequency

text.en: Draft the safety policy with the organisation's commitments, including its stance on reporting.
Have the accountable manager sign and date the policy.
Set safety objectives that follow from the policy and can each be measured.
State the measure, target and reporting frequency for each objective.
Publish the policy and objectives to every member of staff.

title.en: Assign the safety manager and the other key safety personnel

description.en: UAS.LUC.030(2)(d) requires key safety personnel appointed to execute the safety policy. Appoint a safety manager and, where the organisation's size warrants, others such as a safety action group. EASA's guidance lets the accountable manager also act as safety manager, but not where the safety manager also performs the compliance monitoring manager's functions. Record each appointment and the time each role is given.

evidenceHint.en: Appointment letters for the safety manager and other key safety personnel, with a check that no role combination conflicts

text.en: Appoint the safety manager in writing and state the role's duties.
Decide whether the organisation's size needs further key safety personnel or a safety action group.
Check that the accountable manager is not safety manager where that person also monitors compliance.
Record the time allocated to each safety role.

title.en: Run safety training and safety communication for every LUC staff member

description.en: Promote safety through training, education and communication, as UAS.LUC.030(2)(f) requires. Give every member of staff safety training on joining and at intervals, covering the policy, how to report and what happens to reports, and communicate lessons from occurrences and investigations so staff see the system working.

evidenceHint.en: Safety training records per staff member and a log of safety communications issued, such as bulletins and briefings

text.en: Give every new member of staff safety training before they take up safety duties.
Repeat safety training at a set interval and record completion.
Issue lessons learned from occurrences and investigations to staff.
Keep a log of every safety communication issued and who received it.

title.en: Review the safety policy and objectives with the accountable manager each year

description.en: Once a year, the accountable manager and the safety manager review whether the safety policy still fits the organisation and whether each safety objective was met. Objectives met easily may need raising; objectives missed need actions. Changes to the policy or to key safety personnel are recorded, and a significant change to the safety management system needs the competent authority's prior approval.

evidenceHint.en: Annual safety review minutes recording each objective's result, the actions agreed and any change to the policy or safety personnel

text.en: Report each safety objective's result for the year against its target.
Agree actions for objectives missed and revised targets where needed.
Decide whether the safety policy still fits the organisation and amend it if not.
Flag any significant system change for the competent authority's prior approval.
Minute the review and sign it.

templates.title: Safety risk management, safety reporting and management of change
templates.description: The LUC holder identifies safety hazards, evaluates and mitigates their risks and checks the mitigations work, documents the key safety management processes, runs safety reporting and investigations, and obtains approval before changing its terms or its safety management system significantly.
templates.objective: To ensure the LUC holder finds its hazards, treats their risks with mitigations it verifies, learns from reports, and changes its system only with approval where required.
templates.successCriteria:
A hazard log records each identified hazard with its risk evaluation, the mitigation chosen, its owner and the check of its effectiveness.
Each key safety management process is documented with who does what and how the document is amended.
Every safety report received was acknowledged, assessed and, where warranted, investigated, with the outcome fed back.
No change to the terms of approval or significant change to the safety management system took effect without prior approval.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the hazard log and the risk assessments behind it, with the mitigation actions and effectiveness checks.
Obtain the documented key processes of the safety management system and their amendment records.
Obtain the safety report register, the investigation reports and the feedback given to reporters.
Obtain the change log for the terms of approval and the safety management system, and the competent authority's approvals.

Analysis:
Sample hazards and trace each from identification through evaluation and mitigation to a recorded effectiveness check.
Read the documented processes against the nine key processes UAS.LUC.030(2)(g) lists and note any missing or undocumented.
Sample safety reports and confirm each was assessed, investigated where warranted, closed and fed back.
For each change in the log, decide whether it changed the terms or was significant to the safety management system, and confirm prior approval for each such change, including any change of accountable manager.

Output:
A list of hazards without a mitigation or an effectiveness check.
A list of key processes missing or undocumented.
A list of safety reports left unassessed or without feedback, and changes made without the approval they needed.

title.en: Define how the LUC holder identifies hazards and evaluates their safety risks

description.en: Set out the safety risk management method UAS.LUC.030(2)(e) requires: where hazards come from (operations, maintenance, reports, audits, changes, subcontractors), how each risk is evaluated, who decides on mitigation, how actions are tracked and how their effectiveness is verified. Use one risk matrix across the organisation so risks can be compared and prioritised.

evidenceHint.en: Safety risk management procedure with the hazard sources, the risk matrix, decision rights and the effectiveness-check method

text.en: List the sources from which hazards are identified, including reports, audits and changes.
Adopt one risk matrix for likelihood and severity across the organisation.
State who may accept a risk at each level and who decides on mitigations.
Describe how mitigation actions are tracked and how their effectiveness is checked.

title.en: Document the LUC safety management key processes and how each is amended

description.en: UAS.LUC.030(2)(g) requires the key processes documented so personnel know their responsibilities and how the documents are amended: safety reporting and internal investigations, operational control, safety communication, training and safety promotion, compliance monitoring, safety risk management, management of change, interfaces between organisations, and the use of subcontractors and partners. Document each one, including its owner and its amendment route.

evidenceHint.en: Documented key processes, one per UAS.LUC.030(2)(g) item, each with an owner and an amendment procedure

text.en: Document safety reporting and investigation, operational control and safety communication.
Document training and safety promotion, compliance monitoring and safety risk management.
Document management of change, interfaces between organisations and the use of subcontractors.
Name the owner of each process and how its document is amended.
Make each process document available to the personnel it applies to.

title.en: Run safety reporting and internal investigations for each hazard and occurrence report

description.en: Make it easy for anyone to report a hazard or occurrence, acknowledge each report, assess it against the risk matrix and investigate where the risk warrants. Investigations look for causes, not culprits, and end in actions. Tell the reporter what happened to their report. Occurrences that must also go to the competent authority under Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 are reported there as well.

evidenceHint.en: Safety report register showing acknowledgement, assessment, investigation where warranted, actions and feedback for each report

text.en: Acknowledge each safety report to the reporter within a set time.
Assess each report against the risk matrix and decide whether to investigate.
Investigate warranted reports for causes and record the actions agreed.
Send any mandatory occurrence report to the competent authority as well.
Tell each reporter the outcome of their report.

title.en: Verify that each LUC safety mitigation reduced the risk it was taken for

description.en: A mitigation that was carried out is not the same as a mitigation that worked. For each action in the hazard log, set how its effectiveness will be checked, such as a later audit, a trend in reports or a spot check in operations, and record the result. Reopen the risk where the check shows the action did not achieve its aim.

evidenceHint.en: Hazard log entries with each mitigation's effectiveness check, its date and result, and any reopened risk

text.en: Set an effectiveness check for each mitigation when the action is agreed.
Carry out each check when due and record the result in the hazard log.
Reopen the risk and agree further action where a mitigation did not work.
Report overdue checks to the accountable manager.

title.en: Obtain prior approval before changing the LUC terms or significantly changing the safety system

description.en: UAS.LUC.070 requires the competent authority's prior approval for any change to the terms of approval and for any significant change to the safety management system. EASA's guidance treats a change of accountable manager as significant. Run every such change through the management of change process, which assesses its safety effect and records whether prior approval is needed, before it takes effect.

evidenceHint.en: Management of change records showing the safety assessment, the approval decision and, where needed, the competent authority's prior approval

text.en: Route every proposed change to the terms or the safety management system through management of change.
Assess each change's safety effect and record it.
Decide whether the change alters the terms or is significant, treating a new accountable manager as significant.
Apply for prior approval and hold the change until the competent authority grants it.

title.en: Review the LUC hazard log and open safety actions each quarter

description.en: Each quarter, the safety manager reviews the hazard log with the people who own its risks: new hazards since the last review, risks whose level has moved, mitigation actions overdue and effectiveness checks pending. Escalate what is stuck to the accountable manager, so the log is a working tool rather than a register filled once.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly hazard log review record with new hazards, changed risk levels, overdue actions and escalations

text.en: List hazards added and risks whose level changed since the last review.
Identify mitigation actions and effectiveness checks that are overdue.
Agree new due dates or escalate stuck actions to the accountable manager.
Record the review and send it to the risk owners.

templates.title: Independent compliance monitoring, subcontractors and authority access
templates.description: The LUC holder has an independent function that monitors compliance and reports findings to the accountable manager, manages the safety risks of subcontracted services through procedures in its manual, and gives the competent authority access to everything relevant, subcontracted work included.
templates.objective: To ensure the LUC holder's compliance is checked independently, subcontracted safety risks are managed, and the competent authority can reach every relevant record and facility.
templates.successCriteria:
A compliance monitoring function independent of the activities it audits runs a dated audit programme covering the regulation and the LUC manual.
Every compliance finding was reported to the accountable manager with a corrective action, owner and due date, and was closed with evidence.
The LUC manual holds procedures for managing each partner organisation and subcontractor.
Each subcontracted service or product has a recorded safety risk assessment and mitigations.
Every subcontract obliges the subcontractor to give the competent authority access.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the compliance monitoring procedure, the audit programme, audit reports and the findings register with corrective actions.
Obtain the appointment and independence arrangements of the compliance monitoring manager and any auditors used.
Obtain the LUC manual's subcontractor procedures, the list of subcontracted services and products, their risk assessments and the contracts.
Obtain any record of competent authority access or inspection in the period.

Analysis:
Confirm the people auditing an activity do not perform it, and that the programme covers every requirement of Part C and every chapter of the LUC manual over its cycle.
Trace each finding to the report to the accountable manager, the corrective action and its evidence of closure.
Compare the list of subcontracted services and products with the risk assessments held and identify any without one.
Read each subcontract for an access clause covering the competent authority.
Check that any request for access was met in full and in time.

Output:
A statement on the independence of the compliance monitoring function and the coverage of its programme.
A list of findings open past their due date or closed without evidence.
A list of subcontracts lacking a risk assessment or an access clause.

title.en: Establish an independent compliance monitoring function and its audit programme

description.en: UAS.LUC.030(2)(h) requires an independent function that monitors compliance with the regulation and the adequacy of how it is met. Appoint a compliance monitoring manager who may use auditors, keep auditors independent of the activities they audit, and set an audit programme that covers every requirement of Part C and every part of the LUC manual over a set cycle.

evidenceHint.en: Compliance monitoring procedure, the compliance monitoring manager's appointment and an audit programme covering Part C and the LUC manual

text.en: Appoint the compliance monitoring manager in writing.
Record how auditors are kept independent of the activities they audit.
Set an audit programme that covers every Part C requirement and every LUC manual chapter in a cycle.
Schedule the year's audits and assign the auditors.

title.en: Audit LUC compliance and report each finding to the accountable manager

description.en: Carry out the audits in the programme, record findings against the requirement or procedure they breach, and feed every finding back to the accountable manager so corrective measures are actually implemented, as UAS.LUC.030(2)(h) requires. Each finding gets a corrective action, an owner and a due date, and is closed only with evidence that the cause was dealt with.

evidenceHint.en: Audit reports and a findings register with the report to the accountable manager, corrective actions, owners, due dates and closure evidence

text.en: Carry out each audit in the programme and record the evidence examined.
Record each finding against the requirement or procedure it breaches.
Report the findings to the accountable manager with proposed corrective actions.
Assign an owner and a due date to each corrective action.
Close a finding only when evidence shows its cause was addressed.

title.en: Write LUC manual procedures for managing partner organisations and subcontractors

description.en: Where any activity is carried out by a partner organisation or a subcontractor, UAS.LUC.040(3) requires procedures in the LUC manual for how the LUC holder manages the relationship. Cover how a subcontractor is selected and approved, what the contract must contain, how its work is monitored and audited, and how problems are escalated or the arrangement ended.

evidenceHint.en: LUC manual section on partner and subcontractor management, with the contract requirements and the monitoring arrangements

text.en: List every activity carried out by a partner organisation or subcontractor.
Write how subcontractors are selected and approved before work starts.
State the clauses every contract must contain, including access for the competent authority.
Describe how subcontracted work is monitored, audited and escalated.
Add the procedures to the LUC manual through its amendment process.

title.en: Assess and mitigate the safety risks of each subcontracted service or product

description.en: UAS.LUC.030(2)(i) requires a function that makes sure the safety risks of services or products delivered through subcontractors are assessed and mitigated within the operator's own safety management system. For each subcontracted service, such as maintenance, airspace observation, data links or training, assess what could go wrong, how that would affect safety and what mitigation the operator relies on.

evidenceHint.en: Risk assessment per subcontracted service or product, entered in the hazard log with mitigations and owners

text.en: List each service or product delivered through a subcontractor that affects safety.
Assess how a failure of each one could affect the operation's safety.
Record the mitigations relied on and enter the risks in the hazard log.
Reassess when a subcontractor or its service changes.

title.en: Bind subcontractors to give the competent authority access and test the LUC holder's readiness

description.en: UAS.LUC.090 obliges the LUC holder to give any person authorised by the competent authority access to any facility, UAS, document, record, data or procedure relevant to its activity, whether or not that activity is subcontracted. Make sure every subcontract carries the same obligation, keep an index of where everything is held, and test once a year that a request could be met quickly.

evidenceHint.en: Contract review showing an access clause in each subcontract, the document index, and the record of a yearly access dry run

text.en: Check each subcontract for a clause giving the competent authority access.
Amend any contract that lacks the clause at its next renewal or sooner.
Keep an index of where facilities, aircraft, records and procedures are held.
Run a yearly dry run of an access request and record how long it took to meet.

templates.title: LUC manual
templates.description: The LUC holder provides the competent authority with an LUC manual describing its organisation, procedures and activities, carrying the accountable manager's signed commitment, amended to stay current and distributed to staff according to their duties.
templates.objective: To ensure the LUC manual describes the organisation as it actually is, carries the required commitment, and reaches the people who must work to it.
templates.successCriteria:
The LUC manual describes, directly or by cross-reference, the organisation, its procedures and its activities.
The manual contains a statement signed by the accountable manager, countersigned by the chief executive where they are different people, committing to work to the regulation and the approved manual.
Every amendment was sent to the competent authority and the manual matches the organisation as it is today.
Each member of staff holds the parts of the manual relevant to their function and duties.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the current LUC manual, its revision history and the records of amendments sent to the competent authority.
Obtain the signed commitment statement and the organisation chart.
Obtain the distribution matrix showing which parts each function receives, and staff acknowledgements.

Analysis:
Compare the manual's description of the organisation, personnel and procedures with the current organisation chart, appointments and practice, and note differences.
Follow each cross-reference and confirm the document it points to exists in the version cited.
Check the commitment statement's signatures against the current accountable manager and chief executive.
Compare each amendment's date with the date it was sent to the competent authority.
Sample staff and confirm each holds and has acknowledged the parts relevant to their duties.

Output:
A list of differences between the manual and the organisation as it is.
A list of broken cross-references and amendments not sent to the authority.
A statement on the commitment statement's validity and on distribution coverage.

title.en: Map the organisation, procedures and activities the LUC manual must describe

description.en: Before drafting, list what the LUC manual must describe under UAS.LUC.040(1): the organisation, the relevant procedures and the activities carried out. Decide for each item whether the manual describes it directly or cross-refers to another controlled document, such as the operations manual, and note where that document lives and which version it is.

evidenceHint.en: Content map listing each subject the LUC manual covers and whether it is described directly or by cross-reference, with the target document and version

text.en: List the organisation's structure, personnel and their responsibilities.
List the procedures and activities carried out under the LUC.
Decide for each item whether to describe it directly or cross-refer to another document.
Record the document and version each cross-reference will point to.

title.en: Draft the LUC manual and check every cross-reference resolves

description.en: Write the LUC manual from the content map, describing the organisation, the procedures and the activities, and cross-referring where another controlled document already holds the detail. A manual is only as good as its references, so check that each one points to a document that exists in the version cited, and that nothing the manual relies on sits only in someone's head.

evidenceHint.en: Draft LUC manual with a cross-reference check listing each reference, its target document and version, and its status

text.en: Write each section of the LUC manual from the content map.
Insert cross-references to controlled documents where they hold the detail.
Check each cross-reference points to a document that exists in the version cited.
Have the owner of each process review the section that describes it.

title.en: Obtain the accountable manager's signed LUC commitment and the chief executive's countersignature

description.en: UAS.LUC.040(2) requires the manual to contain a statement signed by the accountable manager that the organisation will always work in accordance with the regulation and the approved LUC manual. Where the accountable manager is not the chief executive officer, the chief executive countersigns it. Renew the statement whenever either person changes.

evidenceHint.en: Commitment statement in the LUC manual signed by the accountable manager and, where different, countersigned by the chief executive

text.en: Insert the commitment statement at the front of the LUC manual.
Have the accountable manager sign and date it.
Obtain the chief executive's countersignature where they are a different person.
Renew the statement whenever the accountable manager or chief executive changes.

title.en: Issue the relevant parts of the LUC manual to each function

description.en: UAS.LUC.040(5) requires the relevant parts of the manual distributed to all personnel according to their functions and duties. Build a matrix of which parts each function needs, distribute them in a form people can reach in the field, collect acknowledgements and repeat the distribution with every revision.

evidenceHint.en: Distribution matrix by function and acknowledgement records for the current revision

text.en: Build a matrix showing which manual parts each function needs.
Distribute the parts to each person in a form they can reach where they work.
Collect an acknowledgement from each person for the revision received.
Repeat the distribution and acknowledgement with each new revision.

title.en: Amend the LUC manual and send each amendment to the competent authority

description.en: UAS.LUC.040(4) requires the manual amended as necessary to keep an up-to-date description of the organisation, with copies of amendments provided to the competent authority. Review the manual whenever the organisation, its people or its procedures change and at least once a year, record each amendment and send it to the authority. Changes that are significant or alter the terms need prior approval first.

evidenceHint.en: LUC manual revision history with each amendment's date and the record of its submission to the competent authority

text.en: Review the manual after any change to the organisation, personnel or procedures, and at least yearly.
Amend the affected sections and record the revision number and date.
Check whether the change needs prior approval before it takes effect.
Send a copy of each amendment to the competent authority and file the record.

templates.title: Operational control and self-authorisation of operations
templates.description: The LUC holder exercises operational control over every flight under its certificate and authorises each of its own operations in writing, after an Article 11 risk assessment, only within the privileges and terms of approval it holds.
templates.objective: To ensure every operation an LUC holder authorises itself is within its privileges, rests on a risk assessment and is under the organisation's operational control.
templates.successCriteria:
A documented operational control system states who may start, continue, end or divert a flight in the interest of safety, and how.
Every self-authorised operation has an internal authorisation record signed by the person responsible for authorising operations.
Each internal authorisation cites the privilege relied on and an Article 11 risk assessment, unless a declaration would have sufficed.
No operation outside the LUC's privileges or terms of approval was self-authorised.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the operational control procedure and the operations manual chapter that describes it.
Obtain the internal authorisation records for the period and the risk assessments they cite.
Obtain the terms of approval and the flight log.
Obtain records of operations refused or escalated because they fell outside the privileges.

Analysis:
Read the operational control procedure for who holds authority to initiate, continue, terminate or divert a flight, and how they are trained and reached.
Trace a sample of flights from the flight log to an internal authorisation signed by the person named in the LUC as responsible for authorising operations.
For each sampled authorisation, confirm it cites a privilege in the terms of approval and a current risk assessment, or records why a declaration would have sufficed.
Compare the operations self-authorised with the privileges, types and areas in the terms of approval.
Review refused or escalated operations to confirm the refusal held.

Output:
A list of flights without an internal authorisation or signed by someone else.
A list of authorisations without a privilege or risk assessment.
A list of self-authorised operations outside the terms of approval.

title.en: Define the LUC holder's operational control system

description.en: UAS.LUC.020(3) requires a system for exercising operational control over every operation under the LUC. EASA's guidance reads operational control as responsibility for starting, continuing, ending or diverting a flight in the interest of safety, and the system as the organisation, methods, documents, people and training behind it, described as a chapter of the operations manual. Write who holds that authority, how it is exercised and how those people are trained.

evidenceHint.en: Operational control chapter in the operations manual naming who may initiate, continue, terminate or divert a flight, the methods used and the training required

text.en: Name who holds authority to initiate, continue, terminate or divert a flight.
Describe how that authority is exercised and how those people are reached during operations.
State the training each person with operational control must complete.
Add the description as a chapter of the operations manual.

title.en: Set up an internal authorisation procedure for the LUC holder's own operations

description.en: With the privilege to authorise its own operations (UAS.LUC.060(2)), the organisation stands where the competent authority would. Write an internal procedure that checks, before any authorisation, that the operation falls within a privilege and the terms of approval, that an Article 11 risk assessment supports it unless a declaration would suffice, and that the UAS.SPEC.050 and UAS.SPEC.060 duties are met.

evidenceHint.en: Internal authorisation procedure and form covering the privilege relied on, the risk assessment, the terms of approval and the operator and pilot duties

text.en: Write the steps an operation must pass before it is self-authorised.
Require the privilege relied on and the terms-of-approval item it falls under.
Require a current Article 11 risk assessment, or a record of why a declaration would suffice.
Require confirmation that the operator and remote pilot duties of Part B are met.
Name the person responsible for authorising operations as the only signatory.

title.en: Authorise each own operation in writing before it starts

description.en: No operation under the LUC starts without an internal authorisation signed by the person the LUC names as responsible for authorising operations. The authorisation records the operation, its limits and mitigations, the privilege and risk assessment it rests on and the date it was granted, and it is available to the crew before the flight.

evidenceHint.en: Signed internal authorisation per operation, available to the crew, citing the privilege, risk assessment, limits and mitigations

text.en: Complete the internal authorisation form for each operation before it is planned for flight.
Have the person responsible for authorising operations review and sign it.
Give the signed authorisation to the crew before the first flight.
Link each flight log entry to the authorisation it flew under.

title.en: Escalate any operation outside the LUC holder's privileges instead of authorising it

description.en: An operation the privileges do not cover must not be self-authorised, however urgent. Refuse it, or route it to a declaration or to an application for an operational authorisation from the competent authority. EASA's guidance expects an aircraft with an EASA type certificate for operations at SAIL V and VI, and the authority may require one at SAIL III and IV, so check that too.

evidenceHint.en: Log of operations refused or escalated, with the reason and the route taken, such as a declaration or an authorisation application

text.en: Check each requested operation against the privileges and terms of approval before accepting it.
Refuse any operation that falls outside them and record the reason.
Route a refused operation to a declaration or an authorisation application where it should go ahead.
Check whether the operation's SAIL requires an aircraft with an EASA type certificate.

title.en: Sample the LUC holder's self-authorised operations against their authorisation records

description.en: Each quarter, take a sample of flights from the flight log and check each against its internal authorisation: was it signed in advance by the right person, did it cite a privilege and a current risk assessment, and did the flight stay within the limits and mitigations it set? Raise findings into compliance monitoring.

evidenceHint.en: Quarterly sample worksheet comparing flights with their internal authorisations, and the findings raised

text.en: Select a sample of flights from the quarter's flight log.
Find the internal authorisation for each and check it was signed before the flight.
Check each cited privilege and risk assessment was valid on the flight date.
Compare the flight with the limits and mitigations the authorisation set.
Raise findings into compliance monitoring with owners and due dates.

templates.title: LUC records and continuing validity
templates.description: The LUC holder keeps the risk assessments, mitigations and personnel records behind its self-authorised operations for at least three years, protected from damage, alteration and theft, and keeps its certificate valid through continuing compliance.
templates.objective: To ensure the LUC holder can show, for three years, the basis of every operation it authorised, and that its certificate remains valid and is handled correctly if it ends.
templates.successCriteria:
For every self-authorised operation of the last three years, the risk assessment, its supporting documents and the mitigations taken can be retrieved.
Personnel qualification and experience records are kept for each person's employment and for three years after they leave.
Records are stored with backups and controls that protect them from damage, alteration and theft.
An annual self-assessment confirms continuing compliance with the regulation and with the issuing State's requirements.
templates.testingMethodology:
Evidence:
Obtain the record-keeping procedure, the storage locations and the backup arrangements for LUC records.
Obtain the list of self-authorised operations of the last three years and the personnel list, including leavers.
Obtain the annual validity self-assessment and any surrender or revocation correspondence.

Analysis:
Sample self-authorised operations across the three-year window and retrieve, for each, the risk assessment, its supporting documents and the mitigations taken.
Sample current staff and leavers of the last three years and retrieve each one's qualification and experience records.
Test the protections: restore a record from backup, check who can alter records and whether changes are logged.
Confirm the retention clock is counted from when a record was created or last amended.
Read the self-assessment for coverage of the regulation and of the issuing State's requirements.

Output:
A retrieval table for the sampled operations and personnel, with any record missing or incomplete.
A statement on the effectiveness of the protection and backup controls.
A statement on the LUC's continuing validity and any action needed.

title.en: Define the LUC record set and its three-year retention clock
